definition_zh: 卡车；货车；手推车；用卡车运送
definition_en: a large road vehicle with a strong body for carrying goods, or a small cart pushed by hand
core_image: 一辆满载木箱的大卡车轰隆隆地驶过仓库门口
scene: 仓库门口的坡道上，一辆大车正缓缓倒进来，后厢门放平搭在地上。 A truck loaded with boxes pulled into the yard before six.
sceneCN: 这里 truck 是「卡车；货车」（第 1 个义项：在公路上运货的大型车辆）；句意为一辆装满箱子的卡车六点前开进院子。坡道上缓缓倒车的那个大家伙，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 truck 加 -er 构成，义为「卡车司机」
由 truck 与 load 复合，义为「一卡车的量」
由 truck 加 -ing 构成，义为「卡车运输业」

senses.title: The big goods carrier
senses.definition: a large motor vehicle built to carry heavy loads along roads
senses.definitionCN: 在公路上运送重货的大型机动车
senses.example: A truck loaded with boxes pulled into the yard before six.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆装满箱子的卡车六点前开进院子。
senses.why: The word began as a small wheel and grew into the machine that rides on those wheels.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一只小轮子，后来长成了靠那些轮子行走的机器。

senses.title: The small hand cart
senses.definition: a low open cart with wheels, pushed by hand or pulled by a person
senses.definitionCN: 带轮的低矮敞篷小车，用手推或拉
senses.example: He wheeled a truck of bricks across the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一辆手推车把砖推过院子。
senses.why: Older English used truck for a small wheel, so the little cart named itself after its wheels.
senses.whyCN: 早期英语用 truck 指小轮子，于是那辆小车是以它的轮子命名的。

senses.title: To move by truck
senses.definition: to carry goods in a truck from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 用卡车把货物从一处运到另一处
senses.example: The company trucks fresh vegetables to the city each night.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每晚把新鲜蔬菜用卡车运到城里。
senses.why: Once the vehicle had a name, the verb simply followed: to truck goods is to move them by truck.
senses.whyCN: 车辆有了名字，动词就顺势而生：truck goods 就是用卡车运货。

intro.en: Truck probably comes through French from the Latin trochus, a wheel or hoop, and its first English sense was a small wheel.
intro.cn: truck 大概经法语来自拉丁语 trochus（轮、圈），它在英语里的第一个含义是「小轮子」。

items.en: Trokhos meant a wheel or a circular course.
items.cn: trokhos 意为轮子或环行的路径。

items.en: Trochus named an iron hoop used in games and, later, any wheel.
items.cn: trochus 指游戏用的铁圈，后来泛指轮子。

items.en: Troque named a pulley wheel or a small wooden wheel.
items.cn: troque 指滑轮或小木轮。

items.en: English truck first meant a small wheel, then the low cart that ran on them.
items.cn: 英语 truck 先指小轮，再指靠这些小轮行走的低矮车。

items.en: With engines the cart grew into the heavy road vehicle of today.
items.cn: 有了发动机，那辆车长成了今天公路上的重型车辆。

note.en: The first group shares the truck stem, the second holds other words for goods vehicles.
note.cn: 第一组共享 truck 词干，第二组收其他表示载货车与运货的词。

entries.definition: A person who drives a truck.
entries.definitionCN: 卡车司机

entries.definition: As much as a truck can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 一卡车的量

entries.definition: The business of moving goods by road.
entries.definitionCN: 卡车运输业

entries.definition: The British word for a large goods vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 卡车（英式说法）

entries.definition: A smaller covered vehicle for light loads.
entries.definitionCN: 厢式货车

entries.definition: A small vehicle with wheels, often pulled.
entries.definitionCN: 大车；手推车

normalIntro.en: Truck is a short, blunt word that sounds like the noise of a heavy vehicle on a rough road.
normalIntro.cn: truck 短促粗硬，听起来就像重型车在颠簸路上的声音。

normal.en: The past forms add a k sound: trucked, trucking.
normal.cn: 过去式加 k 音：trucked、trucking。

normal.en: Trucker is the driver, trucking is the business.
normal.cn: trucker 是司机，trucking 是运输业。

normal.en: A truckload says how much the vehicle can hold.
normal.cn: truckload 说明这辆车能装多少。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: trucks.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trucks。

normal.en: The first English meaning was simply a small wheel.
normal.cn: 英语里最早的含义只是「小轮子」。

abstract.en: A back door lowering to the ground like a drawbridge.
abstract.cn: 后门像吊桥一样放下来。

abstract.en: Dust rising behind a heavy load on a dirt road.
abstract.cn: 土路上重车后扬起的尘土。

abstract.en: A single wheel rolling on its own before any cart exists.
abstract.cn: 在有车之前，一只轮子独自滚动。

examples.en: The truck stopped by the river to unload the sand.
examples.cn: 卡车在河边停下卸沙。

examples.en: Farmers truck their milk to the factory before sunrise.
examples.cn: 农民在日出前用卡车把牛奶运到工厂。

examples.en: A truck of hay stood by the barn door.
examples.cn: 一辆装满干草的手推车停在谷仓门口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳克」——大车一开过来，路面被戳得咔咔响，就是卡车。

root: 可能经法语 troque 来自拉丁语 trochus（铁圈、轮子），再上溯希腊语 trokhos；本义「小轮子」，后指手推车、载货卡车；同族词有 trucker、truckload、trucking。

sensesIntro.en: First the heavy road vehicle, then the little hand cart, then the verb of carrying by truck.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是重型公路车辆，再是小手推车，最后是用卡车运送的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a back door lowering onto a loading ramp.
core.cn: 核心意象：后门放下搭到装卸坡上。

branches.en: The vehicle branch: the engine replaced the horse.
branches.cn: 车辆分支：发动机取代了马。

branches.en: The cart branch: the small wheel still survives.
branches.cn: 小车分支：小轮子的影子仍在。

branches.en: The action branch: moving goods by road.
branches.cn: 动作分支：沿公路运送货物。

branches.en: The road branch: the truck and its work share one picture.
branches.cn: 公路分支：车与它的活儿共用一幅画。

branches.en: The wheel branch: both still run on wheels.
branches.cn: 轮子分支：两者都靠轮子行走。

intro.en: Truck is a short free stem that takes -er, -ing and compound forms easily.
intro.cn: truck 是短小的自由词干，容易接 -er、-ing 以及复合形式。

latinIntro.en: The Greek and Latin source trochus, a wheel, also gives the technical words below.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语来源 trochus（轮子）还生出下面的技术词。

items.example: The stem works as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干可作名词与动词。

items.example: It forms trucking, the road freight trade.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trucking，公路货运业。

items.meaning: as much as can be carried
items.example: It forms truckload, one full load.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 truckload，一整车的量。

items.example: The stone was trucked from the quarry.
items.exampleCN: 石头是从采石场用卡车运来的。

items.example: They are trucking the harvest south.
items.exampleCN: 他们正把收成运往南方。

items.example: Fire names the job of the vehicle.
items.exampleCN: fire 说明这辆车的工作。

definition_zh: 力量；权力；能力；电力；幂（数学）；（镜头的）放大倍率
definition_en: the ability to act, control or influence, or the energy and mathematical capacity that make action possible
core_image: 一只手握住总闸的把手往下一压，整条街的灯同时亮起
scene: 变电站里，值班员把总闸推上去，整片街区的灯同时亮了。 A fallen line cut the power to three streets before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里指「供给电器的电力」（第 4 个义项：电力供应）；句意为天亮前一条掉落的电线切断了三条街的供电。可辨识物件：总闸、变电站、电线、街灯、工具箱；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 不可数用法（力量或电力）
可数复数（多种权力或强国）

derivatives.zh: 有效的；强有力的（同出「能」词根）

senses.title: Physical force
senses.definition: the strength or energy that something uses to move, break or hold another thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物用于移动、破坏或固定另一物的力量或能量
senses.example: The storm's power tore the roof from the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴的力量把棚屋的屋顶掀掉了。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'to be able'; the first kind of ability is the brute ability to move matter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「能够」；最基础的能力就是移动物体的蛮力。

senses.title: Control over people and decisions
senses.definition: the capacity to make others act or to determine collective decisions, whether through office, money or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 使他人行动或决定集体事务的能力，可来自职位、金钱或人数
senses.example: The union used its power to stop the layoffs.
senses.exampleCN: 工会动用它的力量阻止了裁员。
senses.why: Ability directed at people becomes influence; whoever can change what others do holds power.
senses.whyCN: 指向他人的能力变成影响力；能改变他人行为的人就握有权力。

senses.title: Capacity to produce an effect
senses.definition: the ability of a thing, substance or person to produce a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 某物、某物质或某人产生特定效果的能力
senses.example: The drug has the power to relieve pain within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能在几分钟内缓解疼痛。
senses.why: The same 'can' is at work here: the question is not who commands but what a thing is able to do.
senses.whyCN: 这里仍是同一个「能」：问题不是谁在下命令，而是某物能够做成什么。

senses.title: Electricity supplied to a place
senses.definition: electric energy supplied to homes, machines or a network
senses.definitionCN: 供给住宅、机器或电网的电能
senses.example: A fallen line cut the power to three streets before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前一条掉落的电线切断了三条街的供电。
senses.why: The industrial age narrowed the general word to the energy that makes machines able to work.
senses.whyCN: 工业时代把这一通用词收窄为让机器得以运转的能量。

senses.title: An exponent in mathematics
senses.definition: the number that shows how many times a base is multiplied by itself
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个底数被自身相乘多少次的数
senses.example: Two raised to the fifth power equals thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 二的五次方等于三十二。
senses.why: Repeated multiplication multiplies capacity, so mathematics named the count of multiplications by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 重复相乘使能力成倍增长，因此数学用同一个词来命名相乘的次数。

senses.title: Magnification of a lens
senses.definition: the factor by which an optical instrument enlarges a distant object
senses.definitionCN: 光学仪器把远处物体放大的倍数
senses.example: A ten-power lens brings the distant ridge into view.
senses.exampleCN: 十倍的镜头把远处的山脊拉到眼前。
senses.why: A lens multiplies the reach of the eye, so its factor is also called its power.
senses.whyCN: 镜头把眼睛的触及范围成倍扩大，因此它的倍数也被称为它的力量。

senses.title: A strong state on the world stage
senses.definition: a country able to influence other states through military, economic or diplomatic capacity
senses.definitionCN: 能通过军事、经济或外交能力影响他国的国家
senses.example: The two powers agreed to limit naval forces in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 两个强国同意限制该地区的海军力量。
senses.why: States are treated as single actors, so the ability to act becomes a nation's power.
senses.whyCN: 国家被当作单一行动者，因此行动的能力就成为一个国家的力量。

senses.title: Legal authority to act for another
senses.titleCN: 代他人行动的法定权限
senses.definition: a legal document or status allowing one person to act on another's behalf
senses.definitionCN: 允许一个人代另一人行动的法定文件或身份
senses.example: The daughter held power of attorney for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 女儿持有父亲的授权委托书。
senses.why: Law borrowed the word for a delegated ability: the agent can act because the principal's capacity has been transferred.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词表示被授予的能力：代理人能行动，是因为本人的能力被转交了过来。

intro.en: Power came through Old French poeir from Vulgar Latin potere, from Latin posse 'to be able', built on potis 'able' and esse 'to be'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: power 经古法语 poeir 来自通俗拉丁 potere，再往上出自拉丁 posse「能够」，由 potis「有能力的」与 esse「是」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Potis meant 'able, capable, powerful'. Its pre-Latin origin is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: potis 意为「有能力的、能干的、有力量的」。它在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Potis plus esse produced posse, the verb 'to be able, can'.
items.cn: potis 加 esse 构成 posse，即动词「能够、可以」。

items.en: Everyday Latin reshaped the verb as potere, which became the ordinary verb for ability in the Romance languages.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁把这个动词改形为 potere，它后来成为罗曼语族中表示能力的常用动词。

items.en: Old French poeir carried both the verb and a noun for ability into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeir 在十三世纪把动词以及表示能力的名词一并带入英语。

items.en: Mathematics adopted the word for an exponent in the sixteenth century, and the electrical sense followed with the power grid in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 数学在十六世纪用这个词指幂指数；随着电网出现，电力义在十九世纪跟进。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of potis is a reconstruction, and no single first citation is fixed for the electrical sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式；电力义也没有唯一的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same 'able' root; group two holds nouns for strength or influence seen from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「能够」词根的词；第二组是从其他角度表示力量或影响力的名词。

entries.definition: Having great strength or influence; the adjective describes what the noun possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有强大力量或影响力的；形容词描述名词所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Having no ability to act or change a situation; it is the direct negation of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 没有能力行动或改变处境的；是这个名词的直接否定。

entries.definition: Means strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument; it shares the Latin root of ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「效力强的」，尤指药物或论证；共享表示能力的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: An ability that exists but has not yet been exercised; it is power still folded up.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未施展的能力；是仍折叠未用的力量。

entries.definition: The physical quality of being strong; it covers muscles and materials rather than decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或结构上的强壮；覆盖肌肉与材料，而非决策。

entries.definition: Physical energy acting on an object, or organized pressure used to compel.
entries.definitionCN: 作用于物体的物理能量，或用来强迫的有组织压力。

entries.definition: Power that is recognized as rightful; power alone can be held without legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认正当的权力；单纯的力量可以在缺乏正当性的情况下被持有。

entries.definition: The ability to change opinions or decisions without direct command.
entries.definitionCN: 不靠直接命令而改变意见或决定的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real 'able' root, the real derivatives and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「能够」词根、真实的派生词与真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'to be able'; every sense is a kind of ability, from moving a roof to lighting a street.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「能够」；每个义项都是一种能力，从掀翻屋顶到点亮街道。

normal.en: The family runs power, powerful, powerless, powerfully, powered, potent and potential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 power、powerful、powerless、powerfully、powered、potent 与 potential。

normal.en: The political phrases are political power, balance of power and the powers.
normal.cn: 政治搭配有政治权力、力量均势与列强。

normal.en: The technical phrases are power supply, nuclear power and to the power of.
normal.cn: 技术搭配有电源、核能与……次方。

normal.en: The legal phrase is power of attorney, where one person acts for another.
normal.cn: 法律搭配是授权委托书，即一个人代另一个人行动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a master switch that lights a whole street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在总闸上，一下点亮整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a number multiplied by itself again and again until it fills the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数反复自乘，直到写满整页。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that lets one person stand in another's shoes at a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名，让一个人在柜台前站进另一个人的位置。

examples.en: The engine's power is measured in kilowatts rather than horses.
examples.cn: 这台发动机的功率用千瓦而非马力来衡量。

examples.en: The committee has no power to change the budget on its own.
examples.cn: 委员会无权自行改变预算。

examples.en: Three to the fourth power is eighty-one.
examples.cn: 三的四次方是八十一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「能够」加「力」——能推动物体、能让人服从、能让灯亮 → 力量、权力、电力

root: power 经古法语来自通俗拉丁 potere，源头是拉丁 posse「能够」= potis「有能力的」+ esse「是」。potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one root idea, 'being able': able to move matter, able to command people, able to produce an effect, able to supply electricity, able to multiply a number, able to enlarge an image, able to act as a state, able to act for another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词根观念「能够」展开：能移动物体、能命令他人、能产生效果、能供电、能使数字成倍、能放大图像、能作为国家行动、能代他人行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a master switch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在总闸上。

branches.en: THE BODY'S ABILITY: force that moves or breaks matter is the first meaning of being able.
branches.cn: 身体的能力：移动或破坏物体的力量，是「能够」的第一层含义。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL ABILITY: a union or a state acts because people and institutions can be made to move.
branches.cn: 社会的能力：工会或国家能行动，是因为可以使人及机构动起来。

branches.en: THE EFFECT: a drug or a word is powerful when it can change a body or a mind.
branches.cn: 效果：药物或言辞之所以有力，是因为它能改变身体或心智。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: the industrial age gave the general word to the energy that runs machines.
branches.cn: 电流：工业时代把这一通用词交给了驱动机器的能量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED AND DELEGATED: an exponent multiplies a number, a lens multiplies sight, and a legal document transfers capacity.
branches.cn: 可计量与可转交：指数使数字成倍，镜头使视力成倍，法律文件则转交能力。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin adjective of ability, the verb 'to be', the compound verb they form and the modern derived family.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示能力的拉丁形容词、表示「是」的动词、由它们合成的动词以及现代派生词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin potis and esse give posse, the source of power; the same stem yields potent, potential and the noun potentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potis 与 esse 构成 posse，也就是 power 的来源；同一词干还衍生 potent、potential 与名词 potentia。

items.example: The adjective supplied the idea of capability.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「有能力」的观念。

items.example: The verb completes the compound meaning 'to be able'.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词补足「能够」的合成含义。

items.example: The Latin verb stated plain ability.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词表示单纯的能力。

items.example: The noun named capacity as a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指作为一种性质的能力。

items.example: The motor lost power on the climb.
items.exampleCN: 马达在爬坡时失去了动力。

items.example: A powerful storm crossed the coast.
The villagers felt powerless against the landslide.
items.exampleCN: 村民面对山体滑坡感到无能为力。

items.example: The speech argued powerfully for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲为这座桥做了有力的论证。

items.example: The shed runs on solar-powered lights.
items.exampleCN: 棚屋使用太阳能驱动的灯。

items.example: The drug is potent at a very low dose.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在很低的剂量下就有效。

definition_zh: 物主；所有者；产权人；业主
definition_en: a person who owns something, especially the person with the legal title to property or the head of a business

senses.title: A person who owns something
senses.definition: a person who has something as property, whether a house, a car or a pet
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为财产持有的人，可以是房子、汽车或宠物
senses.example: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。
senses.why: Owner is own plus -er, the suffix that turns an action into a person, so the word names whoever holds the property.
senses.whyCN: owner 是 own 加 -er，这个后缀把动作变成人，所以这个词指持有那件财产的人。

senses.title: The person with the legal title
senses.definition: the person or company recorded in law as holding title to a property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律记录上持有某项财产所有权的人或公司
senses.example: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。
senses.why: Because the verb own covers legal possession, adding -er produces the party a deed or register points to when ownership is disputed.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词 own 涵盖法律上的持有，加上 -er 就造出契据或登记簿在产权争议中指认的那一方。

senses.title: The head of a business
senses.definition: the person who runs and profits from a shop, company or sports club
senses.definitionCN: 经营一家店铺、公司或体育俱乐部并从中获利的人
senses.example: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。
senses.why: A business is treated as a thing that can be owned, so the same suffix names the person at the top of it, from a corner shop to a football club.
senses.whyCN: 生意被看作可以拥有的一样东西，于是同一个后缀也用来指站在它顶端的人，从街角小店到足球俱乐部都适用。

intro.en: Owner is an English formation from own and the suffix -er; no Latin ancestor is involved, and the word appears in Middle English.
intro.cn: owner 由 own 加后缀 -er 构成的英语词，不涉及拉丁语祖先，中古英语时期已经出现。

items.en: The base is āgan, to have and to hold, with its participle āgen meaning belonging to someone.
items.cn: 词基是 āgan，意为持有、拥有，其分词 āgen 意为「属于某人的」。

items.en: Middle English ownen, to possess, supplied the stem, and the agent suffix -er was added to name the person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ownen（拥有）提供了词干，再加上表示行为者的后缀 -er 用来指人。

items.en: Forms such as ownere appear in records of land and goods, where a named person had to answer for what was held.
items.cn: ownere 这类形式出现在土地与货物的记录里，那里需要一个具名的人为所持之物负责。

items.en: With industry and property law, owner spread to shops, ships and companies, and compounds such as landowner became common.
items.cn: 随着工业与财产法的发展，owner 扩展到店铺、船只和公司，landowner 之类的复合词也变得常见。

items.en: Modern English uses owner for people and ownership for the abstract right, keeping the two endings clearly apart.
items.cn: 现代英语用 owner 指人，用 ownership 指抽象的权利，两个后缀分工清楚。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the base word and the suffixes that rebuild it; the near-meaning group gathers other names for the person who holds property.
note.cn: 形近组沿基础词和重建它的后缀展开；近义组收其他指「持有财产之人」的说法。

abstract.en: Ownership can be sold, lent or fought over, while the owner may change many times.

abstract.en: Every owner is also someone who answers for what happens to the thing owned.
abstract.cn: 每个所有者同时也是那个要为所拥有之物的遭遇负责的人。

definition_en: the thick fatty part of milk; a soft skin lotion; a pale yellowish-white colour

senses.title: The thick fatty part of milk
senses.definition: the thick, pale-yellow fatty layer that rises to the top of milk
senses.definitionCN: 浮到牛奶顶部的淡黄色厚脂肪层
senses.example: Mom poured cold cream over the fresh strawberries.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈把凉奶油浇在新摘的草莓上。
senses.why: The core image is the richest layer sitting on top of milk, so cream is the heavy white part that floats up.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是最浓的那层浮在牛奶上，所以 cream 就是那层上浮的厚白脂肪。

senses.title: A smooth skin lotion
senses.definition: a smooth substance rubbed on the skin to protect or clean it
senses.definitionCN: 涂在皮肤上保护或清洁的光滑膏体
senses.example: This winter hand cream stops my skin from cracking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种冬季护手霜防止我的皮肤开裂。
senses.why: Thick white cream from milk and thick white lotion for skin look and feel alike, so the name moved across.
senses.whyCN: 牛奶里的厚白奶油和护肤的厚白膏体看起来手感都相似，所以名称迁移了过去。

senses.title: A pale yellowish-white colour
senses.definition: a very pale yellowish-white colour like fresh cream
senses.definitionCN: 像新鲜奶油一样的浅黄白色
senses.example: She painted her bedroom walls a soft cream colour.
senses.exampleCN: 她把卧室墙刷成了柔和的奶油色。
senses.why: Once the dairy word was fixed, its colour became a colour name, like orange and rose.
senses.whyCN: 乳品义固定后，它的颜色也成了颜色名，就像 orange 和 rose。

senses.title: The best part of a group
senses.definition: the best people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一群人里最优秀的那部分
senses.example: The three winners were the cream of this year's contest.
senses.exampleCN: 三位获奖者是今年比赛的佼佼者。
senses.why: The top layer is the richest part, so the best of any group is its cream.
senses.whyCN: 最上层是最浓的部分，所以任何群体里最好的那部分就是它的 cream。

intro.en: Cream came into English through French from a late Latin word about churned milk.
intro.cn: cream 经由法语进入英语，来自晚期拉丁语中与搅乳有关的词。

items.en: Late Latin had cramum or chrisma, a word thought to mean the churned fatty layer of milk.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语有 cramum 或 chrisma 一词，一般认为指搅乳得到的脂肪层。

items.en: Old French carried it as creme, meaning the fatty top of milk.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 creme，指牛奶上层的脂肪。

items.en: English borrowed creme in the fourteenth century for the milk layer.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 creme，指牛奶的脂肪层。

items.en: The sense spread to skin creams and the colour cream.
items.cn: 词义扩展到护肤膏和奶油色。

items.en: Phrases like cream of the crop now mark the best of anything.
items.cn: 像 cream of the crop 这样的短语如今用来指任何事物的精华。

note.en: These words sit near cream in the dairy family or in sound.

intro.cn: anywhere 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It gives the sense of place.
It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.

It names the doer of an action.

definition_zh: 生产；制造；产生；出示；排演；农产品
definition_en: to make, grow or bring something into existence; as a noun, farm products
core_image: 果园枝头的果子被摘进篮子，篮子上贴着产地标签
scene: 农户把今年收的果子装筐，运到镇上的集市。 The farm produces enough apples to fill a stall at the town market.
sceneCN: 农户把今年收的果子装筐运到镇上集市；句中的 produces 指「种出、出产某物」（第 2 个义项：以种植或养殖方式产出）。图中可辨识物件：果园、果筐、集市摊位、产地标签；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生产；制造；产生；出示；排演
农产品（重音移到第一音节）

senses.title: Make or manufacture
senses.definition: to make something, especially in a factory or by a process
senses.definitionCN: 造出某物，尤指在工厂或经某一过程
senses.example: The plant produces parts for wind turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产风力涡轮机的零件。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead forward, so making is bringing material forward into a finished thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前引出」，因此制造就是把材料引成成品。

senses.title: Grow or yield from land
senses.definition: to grow crops or raise animals as a result of farming
senses.definitionCN: 通过耕作或养殖产出作物或畜禽
senses.example: The farm produces enough apples to fill a stall at the town market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场种的苹果足够装满镇上集市的一个摊位。
senses.why: A field yielding fruit is the same bringing-forth, with land rather than a machine doing the work.
senses.whyCN: 田地结出果实也是同一种「带出」，只是出力的是土地而非机器。

senses.title: Cause an effect
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或存在
senses.example: The new policy produced a sharp fall in complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策使投诉量大幅下降。
senses.why: Once anything can be brought forth, the word covers results that are not physical objects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何东西都能被「带出」，这个词便涵盖并非实物的结果。

senses.title: Show or bring forward
senses.definition: to present something for inspection, such as a document or a ticket
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拿出来供查验，如文件或票据
senses.example: The witness produced the original receipt.
senses.exampleCN: 证人出示了原始收据。
senses.why: Bringing something before someone is a literal leading forward, which explains the legal use.
senses.whyCN: 把东西带到某人面前，字面上就是「向前引出」，这解释了法律用法。

senses.title: Stage a play or film
senses.definition: to prepare and present a play, film or show for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 筹备并向观众呈现戏剧、电影或节目
senses.example: The company will produce the play in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 剧团将在春天排演这部戏。
senses.why: A show is brought out before an audience, so the cultural sense keeps the forward direction.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏被带到观众面前，因此文化义保留了「向前」的方向。

senses.title: Generate energy
senses.definition: to generate power, heat or another form of energy
senses.definitionCN: 发出电力、热量或其他形式的能量
senses.example: The dam produces power for three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大坝为三个省发电。
senses.why: Energy is led out of a source into a usable current, which fits the word's movement image.
senses.whyCN: 能量从源头被引出成可用的电流，正合这个词的「引出」意象。

senses.title: Farm products as a mass noun
senses.titleCN: 作不可数名词指农产品
senses.definition: fresh food grown on farms, sold as a group rather than counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 农场种出的新鲜食物，作为整体出售而非逐件计数
senses.example: The shop buys its produce from nearby growers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店从附近农户采购农产品。
senses.why: The verb's result became a collective noun for what the land brings forth.
senses.whyCN: 动词的结果转成了集合名词，指土地带出的东西。

senses.title: The fresh-food section of a shop
senses.definition: the fruit and vegetable section of a shop, or its stock
senses.definitionCN: 商店的果蔬区或其存货
senses.example: The produce aisle was restocked before opening.
senses.exampleCN: 开门前生鲜区补好了货。
senses.why: Retail narrows the collective noun to one department, the place where farm goods are sold.
senses.whyCN: 零售把集合名词收窄为一个部门，即卖农产品的地方。

intro.en: Produce comes from Latin producere 'to lead forward, bring out', through French. The noun for farm goods is a later English development of the same word.
intro.cn: produce 经法语来自拉丁 producere「向前引出、带出」；指农产品的名词义是同一词在英语中的后起发展。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. It gives duct, conduct, reduce and educate.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生 duct、conduct、reduce 与 educate。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere produced producere, 'to lead forward, bring out, bring forth'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere，意为「向前引出、带出」。

items.en: Old French produire carried the verb into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 produire 在十五世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century produce could mean bring forward a document as well as bring goods into being.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，produce 既可指造出货物，也可指出示文件。

items.en: The mass noun for crops and fresh food appeared later, first in English rather than in Latin.
items.cn: 指作物与新鲜食物的不可数名词出现更晚，是英语自身的发展而非拉丁语原有。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the farm noun is not firmly recorded, and the year is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：农产品名词的最早年代没有确切记录，给出的年份只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words constantly confused with produce; group two holds near verbs for making and yielding.
note.cn: 第一组是同根且常与 produce 混淆的词；第二组是表示制造与产出的近义动词。

entries.definition: The thing made; produce as a verb makes products but never names them.
entries.definitionCN: 造出来的东西；作动词的 produce 制造产品，却不用它来指产品。

entries.definition: The activity or total output; it is what happens while produce is what is done.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或总产出；produce 是动作，production 是过程或总量。

entries.definition: The person or firm that makes; the verb names the act, not the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 制造的人或企业；动词指动作，不指施动者。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus produce: to make a copy or to breed; it repeats rather than originates.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再」加 produce：复制或繁殖；是重复而非原创。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for creating something; it is neutral in register where produce is formal.
entries.definitionCN: 创造某物的日常动词；语体中性，而 produce 较正式。

entries.definition: Making goods industrially; it rules out crops and effects, which produce allows.
entries.definitionCN: 工业制造货物；排除作物与结果，而 produce 都允许。

entries.definition: Producing power, data or ideas; it is close in sense three and six but rarer for goods.
entries.definitionCN: 产生电力、数据或想法；接近第 3、6 义，但少用于货物。

entries.definition: To give a crop or a result, often under pressure; it is the farming half of produce.
entries.definitionCN: 出产作物或结果，常含受压之意；是 produce 中务农的一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the lead-forward root, the mass noun and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「向前引出」词根、不可数名词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead': to produce is to lead something into being.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：produce 就是把某物引出来。

normal.en: The family runs produce, product, production, producer, productive and reproduce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、product、production、producer、productive 与 reproduce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: produce evidence, produce results, farm produce, locally produced.
normal.cn: 固定说法：出示证据、产生结果、农产品、本地生产的。

normal.en: The noun shifts its stress to the first syllable, which is how English marks the change of word class.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音移到第一音节，这是英语标记词性变化的方式。

normal.en: The same root appears in conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate 中。

abstract.en: Picture a tree handing fruit into a basket one branch at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树一根枝一根枝地把果子交进篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a document sliding across a desk to be checked.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件在桌面上滑过去接受查验。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns a river's weight into light in a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，把河流的重量变进房间的灯光。

examples.en: The region produces more olive oil than it can sell at home.
examples.cn: 该地区生产的橄榄油超过本地能卖出的量。

examples.en: The lawyer asked the company to produce the missing records.
examples.cn: 律师要求公司出示缺失的记录。

examples.en: A single change in the wording produced a very different response.
examples.cn: 措辞上的一处改动引出了很不一样的反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duce（引导）」——把东西一路引出来，就是生产与出产

root: 拉丁 producere「向前引出、带出」= pro-（向前）+ ducere「引导」；经古法语 produire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bringing-forth: manufacturing, farming, causing an effect, showing a document, staging a show, generating power, farm goods as a mass noun and finally the shop's fresh section.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「带出」这个动作：制造、种出、引起结果、出示文件、排演、发电、作不可数名词指农产品，最后是商店的生鲜区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of picked fruit carrying a label that says where it grew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篮摘下的果子，标签上写着它长在哪里。

branches.en: MAKING AND GROWING: a factory line and a field are both ways of leading material into a result.
branches.cn: 制造与种植：工厂流水线与田地，都是把材料引成结果的方式。

branches.en: BROUGHT FORTH: an effect and a document are both brought forward where they can be seen.
branches.cn: 被带出：结果与文件都被带到能被看见的地方。

branches.en: STAGE AND SHOP: a show and a fresh-food aisle are places where produce is presented to the public.
branches.cn: 舞台与店铺：演出与生鲜区，都是把出产呈现给公众的场所。

branches.en: POWER: energy is led out of a source into a current.
branches.cn: 电力：能量从源头被引出成电流。

branches.en: MASS NOUN: what the land brings forth becomes a collective name for food.
branches.cn: 集合名词：土地带出的东西成了食物的统称。

intro.en: Produce is a Latin verb of leading forward, and its prefix and root still build a large English family.
intro.cn: produce 是表示「向前引出」的拉丁动词，其前缀与词根仍构成一大片英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct, introduce, reduce and educate; pro- adds the forward direction kept in produce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate；pro- 增添 produce 保留的向前方向。

items.example: The prefix points the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向外。

items.example: The product sells in six countries.

definition_zh: 切；割；剪；削减；伤口；剪辑
definition_en: to divide or open something with a sharp tool; to reduce; a wound or editing choice
core_image: 锋利的刃口把一样东西分成两半
scene: 手工课上剪刀咔嚓咔嚓，碎纸像雪花一样落下。 Please cut the paper into eight equal pieces for the origami task.
sceneCN: 这里 cut 是「剪；切」（第 1 个义项：用锋利的工具把东西分开）；句意是请把纸剪成八等份做折纸。

derivatives.zh: 由 cut 加 -ing 构成，义为「锋利的；刺骨的」
由 hair 加 cut 构成，义为「理发；发型」
由 short 加 cut 构成，义为「捷径」

senses.title: Divide with a sharp edge
senses.definition: to use a knife, scissors or another sharp edge to open or divide something
senses.definitionCN: 用刀、剪刀等利刃把东西割开或分开
senses.example: Cut the apple in half before you share it.
senses.exampleCN: 分享苹果之前先把它切成两半。
senses.why: A sharp edge forces things apart, so forcing apart with a blade is the root image.
senses.whyCN: 锋利的刃口能把东西强行分开，用刀刃分开东西正是这个词的根本意象。

senses.title: Reduce an amount
senses.definition: to make a price, number or amount smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、数量或数额变小
senses.example: The school cut the lunch price by two yuan this term.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期学校把午餐价格降低了两元。
senses.why: Removing a slice makes the rest smaller, so cutting a piece from a sum means reducing it.
senses.whyCN: 切掉一片剩下的就变小，所以从总额上「切」一块就是削减。

senses.title: Leave out or remove
senses.definition: to remove a part from a text, film or speech
senses.definitionCN: 从文章、影片或讲话中删去一部分
senses.example: The editor cut three seconds of noise from the video.
senses.exampleCN: 剪辑师从视频里剪掉了三秒的杂音。
senses.why: Slicing away film or words is still dividing with a blade, now done in editing.
senses.whyCN: 剪掉胶片或字句仍是用「刀」分开东西，只是搬到了编辑工作里。

senses.title: A wound or slice in a surface
senses.definition: a break or opening made in the skin or in a surface
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤或表面被割开的裂口
senses.example: The nurse cleaned the small cut on my knee.
senses.exampleCN: 护士清理了我膝盖上的小伤口。
senses.why: The result of the action takes the same name as the action itself.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果与动作共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Cut is a short English word whose early source is uncertain.
intro.cn: cut 是个简短的英语词，早期来源不确定。

items.en: The verb cutten appears in the thirteenth century, meaning to divide with a sharp edge.
items.cn: 十三世纪出现动词 cutten，意为用利刃分开东西。

items.en: Some scholars link it to Old French couteau (knife) or to Old English cyttan; no theory is fully accepted.
items.cn: 有学者把它与古法语 couteau（刀）或古英语 cyttan 联系起来，但没有一种说法被完全接受。

items.en: The noun cut followed, naming the act and the wound it leaves.
items.cn: 名词 cut 随之出现，指切割动作及其留下的伤口。

items.en: The verb spread to prices, film editing and card dealing.
items.cn: 动词的含义扩展到降价、影片剪辑和发牌。

items.en: Compounds like haircut and shortcut made the word part of daily life.
items.cn: haircut、shortcut 之类的复合词让这个词融入了日常生活。

note.en: These words name sharp actions on objects or related reductions.
note.cn: 这些词指用利刃对物体进行的动作或相关的削减。

entries.definition: sharp or biting; also a piece of a plant grown again
entries.definitionCN: 锋利的；扦插枝条

entries.definition: the style or act of cutting hair
entries.definitionCN: 理发；发型

entries.definition: a quicker way to go or to do something
entries.definitionCN: 捷径

entries.definition: a young animal; spelled close to cut, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 幼兽（拼写近似，词义无关）

entries.definition: a common pet animal; only one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 猫（仅一字母之差，词义无关）

entries.definition: to cut into thin flat pieces
entries.definitionCN: 切成薄片

entries.definition: to cut with heavy blows, as with an axe
entries.definitionCN: 砍；剁

entries.definition: to cut small bits off to tidy the shape
entries.definitionCN: 修剪

entries.definition: to cut wood or stone into a shape
entries.definitionCN: 雕刻

entries.definition: to cut violently with long strokes
entries.definitionCN: 猛砍；大幅削减

normalIntro.en: Remember the family of compounds and the three verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 记住复合词家族和三个动词形式。

normal.en: cut-cut-cut: the past and participle never change.
normal.cn: cut 的过去式和过去分词都不变：cut-cut-cut。

normal.en: But the -ing form doubles the t: cutting.
normal.cn: 但 -ing 形式要双写 t：cutting。

normal.en: hair + cut = haircut; short + cut = shortcut.
normal.cn: hair + cut ＝ haircut（理发）；short + cut ＝ shortcut（捷径）。

normal.en: cut down means to fell trees; cut in means to interrupt or jump the queue.
normal.cn: cut down 指砍倒；cut in 指插话或插队。

normal.en: cut the price means to lower it, not to damage money.
normal.cn: cut the price 指降价，不是破坏钱。

abstract.en: Hear the scissors go snip snip and see two paper halves fall.
abstract.cn: 听剪刀咔嚓两声，看两半纸片落下。

abstract.en: Picture an eraser shaving a number smaller and smaller.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮把一个数字越擦越小。

abstract.en: Feel the sting of a paper edge on your finger; that line is a cut.
abstract.cn: 体会纸边划过手指的刺痛，那道线就是伤口。

examples.en: Cut the ribbon, and the new library is open.
examples.cn: 剪断彩带，新图书馆就开放了。

examples.en: He got a cut on his hand while cooking dinner.
examples.cn: 他做晚饭时手上划了个口子。

examples.en: They cut the boring scene from the school play video.
examples.cn: 他们把学校演出视频里无聊的场景剪掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡特」——刀口「卡」进东西里，东西就「特」别干脆地分开了

root: 来源不确定：一般认为与古法语 couteau（刀）或古英语表示切割的词有关，尚无定论；中古英语 cutten 已指「用利刃分开」，后扩展为削减、剪辑与伤口。

sensesIntro.en: One sharp edge gives four meanings: divide, reduce, remove and wound.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一把利刃给出四个意思：分开、削减、删除和伤口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp edge forcing one thing into two
core.cn: 核心意象：锋利的刃口把一样东西分成两半

branches.en: Scissors, knives and paper
branches.cn: 剪刀、刀和纸

branches.en: Lower prices and smaller budgets
branches.cn: 降价和缩减预算

branches.en: Editing film and texts
branches.cn: 剪辑影片和删改文章

branches.en: A line on the skin
branches.cn: 皮肤上的一道伤口

branches.en: Slicing and slicing out
branches.cn: 切开与剪掉是同一动作

intro.en: Cut is a bare root that loves to form compounds.
intro.cn: cut 是个光杆词根，特别爱构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is English to the bone.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，这个词彻头彻尾来自英语本身。

items.meaning: to divide with a sharp edge
an act or style of cutting hair

items.exampleCN: take a shortcut home（抄近路回家）
a pair of scissors（一把剪刀）

items.meaning: the sharp edge of a knife
to cut a shape from material
items.exampleCN: carve a pumpkin face（刻南瓜脸）

definition_zh: 出现；似乎；露面
definition_en: to come into sight, or to seem to be something, or to be seen in public
core_image: 海平线上一条船慢慢浮现
scene: 海平线上先是一个小点，接着一条船出现了。 A boat appeared on the horizon.
sceneCN: 这里 appeared 是「出现」（第 1 个义项：进入视野）；句意为海平线上出现了一条船。

senses.title: To come into sight
senses.definition: to come into view so that it can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 进入视野，能被看见
senses.example: A boat appeared on the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 海平线上出现了一条船。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to come into view, so becoming visible is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为进入视野，所以变得可见就是第一义。

senses.title: To seem
senses.definition: to seem to be something, as far as one can tell
senses.definitionCN: 就人所能判断而言，看起来是某种样子
senses.example: He appears calm, but he is worried.
senses.exampleCN: 他看起来很平静，其实很担心。
senses.why: What comes into view is what people judge by, so the word shifts from being seen to seeming.
senses.whyCN: 进入视野的东西正是人判断的依据，于是词义从「被看见」转为「看起来」。

senses.title: To be seen in public
senses.definition: to be seen in public or to take part in a show
senses.definitionCN: 在公众场合露面或参加演出
senses.example: She appeared in a school play.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一场校园剧里露面了。
senses.why: A person who steps before an audience also comes into view, which gives the public sense.
senses.whyCN: 走到观众面前的人也进入视野，于是有公开露面的义项。

items.cn: apparere 意为进入视野或变得可见。

items.en: Parere meant to come forth or to show itself.
items.cn: parere 意为出现或显露自身。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入日常使用。

items.en: English used appear for something coming into sight.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪用 appear 指某物进入视野。

items.en: Today it also covers seeming and performing.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖「似乎」与「演出」。

normal.en: ad- means toward and parere means to come into view: to appear is to come before the eyes.
normal.cn: ad- 表示朝向，parere 表示显现：appear 就是来到眼前。

normal.en: The same family also gives appearance and apparent.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 appearance 与 apparent。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase appear on stage.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「登台演出」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of appear in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 appear 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to come into sight, or to seem to be something, or to be seen in public.

abstract.cn: 想象海平线上一条船慢慢浮现。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: A boat appeared on the horizon.

examples.en: He appears calm, but he is worried.
examples.cn: 他看起来很平静，其实很担心。

definition_zh: 举起；抬高；提升（精神）；电梯；搭便车
definition_en: to raise something to a higher position; to raise one\u0027s spirits; a machine that carries people up a building; a free ride in a car
core_image: 双手把重物从地面托到空中
scene: 搬家日，他把纸箱从地板托过肩头。 Could you give me a lift to the station?
sceneCN: 这里 lift 是名词「搭便车」（第 6 个义项：免费搭乘）；句意为能顺路捎我去车站吗。

collocations.zh: 让某人搭便车；鼓舞某人

derivatives.zh: lift 加施事后缀 -er，指「举重者；起重装置」
up 与 lift 合成，指「提升；鼓舞」
lift 与 off 合成，指「（火箭）发射升空」

senses.title: To raise to a higher position
senses.definition: to move something up to a higher place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物移到更高的位置
senses.example: She lifted the box onto the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子抬上架子。
senses.why: Gravity must be beaten for a moment, and the word pictures the upward push.
senses.whyCN: 必须短暂战胜重力，词画出了向上的托举。

senses.title: To raise emotions or spirits
senses.definition: to make someone feel happier or more hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使人心更愉快、更有希望
senses.example: The news lifted everyone\u0027s mood.
senses.exampleCN: 消息让所有人的心情一振。
senses.why: Feelings rise like objects: joy lifts, sadness sinks.
senses.whyCN: 情绪如物体升降：喜升而忧沉。

senses.title: To remove or end
senses.definition: to officially remove a rule, block or restriction
senses.definitionCN: 正式取消规则、封锁或限制
senses.example: The city lifted the curfew.
senses.exampleCN: 城市解除了宵禁。
senses.why: Removing a block is lifting the weight that held things down.
senses.whyCN: 解除禁令就是抬起压着东西的重量。

senses.title: To carry people between floors
senses.definition: to move people between floors of a building, or the machine itself
senses.definitionCN: 在楼层间载运人，或指电梯本身
senses.example: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 乘电梯到五楼。
senses.why: The machine does the lifting for you, so it borrowed the verb as a name.
senses.whyCN: 机器替你完成「举」，便借动词作名字。

senses.title: A free ride in a car
senses.definition: a journey in someone else\u0027s car without payment
senses.definitionCN: 免费搭乘他人汽车
senses.example: He gave me a lift home in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨天他捎我回家。
senses.why: The car "lifts" you along the road, so the ride took the name.
senses.whyCN: 汽车把你「抬」着沿路走，旅程便得了这个名。

senses.title: To steal or copy
senses.definition: to take words or ideas from somewhere and use them as one\u0027s own
senses.definitionCN: 把他处文字或点子拿来当作自己的
senses.example: Someone lifted two paragraphs from my draft.
senses.exampleCN: 有人从我草稿里抄了两段。
senses.why: Taking content is "lifting" it out of its place, and the shade is dishonest.
senses.whyCN: 把内容从原处「拿走」，色彩偏负面。

senses.title: Aircraft rising force
senses.definition: the upward force that keeps an aircraft in the air
senses.definitionCN: 使飞行器留在空中的向上之力
senses.example: Wing design increases lift.
senses.exampleCN: 机翼设计可增加升力。
senses.why: Air pushes the plane up just as hands push a box up.
senses.whyCN: 空气托起飞机，正如双手托起箱子。

intro.en: Lift comes from Old Norse lypta 'to raise', from Germanic roots of raising; English took it from the settlers and it grew many senses.
intro.cn: lift 来自古诺斯语 lypta「举起」，出自日耳曼「抬升」词根；英语从定居者处借得并衍生多义。

items.en: Old Norse lypta meant 'to lift, raise' and settled into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lypta 意为「举起」，落脚于英格兰北部。

items.en: The Norse verb belongs to a Germanic raising family, kin to German lüpfen.
items.cn: 诺斯动词属日耳曼「抬升」词族，与德语 lüpfen 有亲缘。

items.en: In Middle English lift spread from hands to spirits and rules.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lift 从双手扩展到情绪与规则。

items.en: Modern English added the elevator name, the free ride, plagiarism and aviation senses.
items.cn: 现代英语新增电梯名、搭便车、剽窃与航空义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the deeper origin of the raising family beyond Germanic is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：抬升词族在日耳曼语之前的来源有争议。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists raising words.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出抬升之词。

entries.definitionCN: 举重者或起重装置。

entries.definition: To lift and set in a higher place; lift stresses the effort.
entries.definitionCN: 抬起并置于高处；lift 强调费力。

entries.definition: To lift heavy things with ropes or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用绳索或机械吊起重物。

entries.definition: To lift or pull with great effort.
entries.definitionCN: 用力举或拉。

entries.definitionCN: 美式说法，对应英式 lift。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用诺斯词根与真实短语。

abstract.cn: 想象杠铃从地面颤抖着升起。

abstract.en: Picture grey clouds parting and one sunbeam lifting the street.
abstract.cn: 想象乌云裂开，一束光提振了整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a thumb up at the roadside, a car slowing down.
abstract.cn: 想象路边竖起的拇指，一辆车缓缓停下。

examples.en: He lifted the sleeping child out of the car.
examples.cn: 他把睡着的孩子从车里抱出来。

examples.en: The government lifted the ban on night flights.
examples.cn: 政府解除了夜航禁令。

examples.en: Reading that poem lifted my spirits for days.
examples.cn: 那首诗让我振奋了好几天。

sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项一路向上：双手、情绪、禁令、乘客、楼层、被抄的文字与天上的机翼。

definition_zh: 曾经；从来；在任何时候；永远；究竟（用于强调）
definition_en: at any time; always; used for emphasis in questions and negatives
core_image: 无限延伸的时间线：任何一点都算数
scene: 爷爷翻着旧相册说这是他见过最亮的星空。 It was the brightest star he had ever seen.
sceneCN: 这里 ever 是「曾经」（第 1 个义项：在任何时候）；句意是他从未见过这么亮的星。

derivatives.zh: 由 ever 加 green 构成，义为「常绿树；常绿的」
由 ever 加 lasting 构成，义为「永恒的；持久的」
由 how 加 ever 构成，义为「然而；无论如何」

senses.title: At any time
senses.definition: at any time, used especially in questions and negative sentences
senses.definitionCN: 在任何时候，尤用于疑问句与否定句
senses.example: Have you ever visited the Great Wall?
senses.exampleCN: 你曾经游览过长城吗？
senses.why: The Old English root means always, so the question sweeps across the whole timeline.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词根意为「永远」，疑问因此扫过整条时间线。

senses.title: Always, continually
senses.definition: all the time, or again and again, often in ever since or for ever
senses.definitionCN: 一直，或一次次，常见于 ever since 与 for ever
senses.example: We have been friends ever since primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们从小学起一直是朋友。
senses.why: When the sweep never ends, the any-time word hardens into an always word.
senses.whyCN: 当扫掠没有终点，「任何时刻」便固化为「一直」。

senses.title: Used for emphasis
senses.definition: used after words like what, how or why to add surprise or force
senses.definitionCN: 放在 what、how、why 等词后加强惊讶或力度
senses.example: Why ever did you hide the keys there?
senses.exampleCN: 你究竟为什么把钥匙藏在那里？
senses.why: Stretching the timeline wide makes any answer seem astonishing.
senses.whyCN: 把时间线拉到最宽，任何答案都显得惊人。

senses.title: Comparative reinforcement
senses.definition: used after superlatives to mean at any time so far
senses.definitionCN: 用在最高级后表示迄今为止任何时候
senses.example: It was the best meal we had ever cooked.
senses.exampleCN: 那是我们做过的最好的一餐。
senses.why: The best of all time is found by sweeping every moment once.
senses.whyCN: 把每一时刻都扫一遍，才能选出有史以来最佳。

intro.en: Ever is an Old English compound of ae meaning ever and a related root for time, literally 'always in time'. It is the same root family as evening.
intro.cn: ever 是古英语复合词，意为「在任何时候」，与 evening 同属「渐成、时间」词族。

items.en: Old English aefre meant 'ever, at any time', built from roots about time and becoming.
items.cn: 古英语 aefre 意为「永远、任何时候」，由关于时间与渐成的词根构成。

items.en: Middle English ever spread into questions, negatives and emphatic phrases.
items.cn: 中古英语 ever 扩展到疑问句、否定句与强调短语。

items.en: Ever since and for ever became fixed phrases in this period.
items.cn: ever since 与 for ever 在这一时期成为固定短语。

items.en: Compound adjectives like ever-growing and evergreen kept the sense of continuation.
items.cn: ever-growing 与 evergreen 等复合词保留了延续之意。

items.en: The emphatic use, why ever not, became common in spoken English.
items.cn: 强调用法 why ever not 在英语口语中变得常用。

note.en: The first group collects the ever-compound family; the second collects near meanings about time.
note.cn: 第一组收集 ever 复合词族；第二组收集与时间相关的近义词。

entries.definition: each one of a group; historically a fusion of ever plus each
entries.definitionCN: 每一个。历史上由 ever 与 each 融合而来，形近义异。

entries.definition: the late-day time; a true cousin sharing the old root of becoming
entries.definitionCN: 晚上；同根真表亲，共享「渐成」词根。

entries.definition: to cut off; only the letters resemble, root is Latin
entries.definitionCN: 切断。仅拼写相似，词根是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 运气；好运；侥幸；时运
definition_en: the force that seems to decide events by chance; also good fortune and success that comes without skill
core_image: 一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时正好卡在指尖上方，摇摇欲坠却没有倒
scene: 码头边，渔夫把最后一网兜拉上来，网里空空的，可转身时却在木板上看见一枚别人掉下的硬币。 Luck came to him at the very moment he had stopped expecting anything.
sceneCN: 这里 luck 是「好运、幸运」（第 2 个义项：带来好结果的好运）；句意为运气在他不再期待的时候降临。画面里可认出码头、空网兜与木板上的硬币。

senses.title: Chance seen as a force that shapes events
senses.definition: the force that seems to decide events by chance, whether the outcome is good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 似乎在冥冥中决定事情成败的偶然力量，无论结果是好是坏
senses.example: No one can explain why the storm missed the village; they put it down to luck.
senses.exampleCN: 谁也说不清风暴为什么绕过了村子，他们把它归因于运气。
senses.why: When people cannot explain why a plan succeeds or fails, they name the unknown cause luck, so the word first stands in for chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说不清一个计划为何成功或失败时，就把这个未知的原因叫作 luck，所以这个词最初是「偶然本身」的代称。

senses.title: Good fortune that brings favourable results
senses.definition: good fortune, especially when it brings success, safety or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 尤指带来成功、平安或优势的好运气
senses.example: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。
senses.why: Because people most often speak of luck when things turn out well, the neutral force narrowed into the favourable sense that dominates everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们通常在事情顺利时才提起 luck，这个中性的力量就收窄成日常最常用的「好运气」义。

senses.title: Success that comes by chance rather than skill
senses.definition: a favourable result that happened by accident rather than through skill or planning
senses.definitionCN: 凭偶然而非技巧或计划取得的有利结果
senses.example: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。
senses.why: If good fortune can deliver a result, then a result delivered that way is itself called luck, so the cause and the outcome share one word.
senses.whyCN: 如果好运能带来结果，那么以这种方式得到的结果本身也被叫作 luck，于是原因与结果共用同一个词。

senses.title: One's personal fortune at a particular time
senses.definition: the state of a person's fortune at a given moment, which can rise or fall
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某一时刻的运气状态，可升可降
senses.example: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
senses.exampleCN: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。
senses.why: Luck as a force can also be treated as something a person possesses, so English speaks of someone's luck rising, falling or running out.
senses.whyCN: 作为力量的 luck 也可以被看成一个人所拥有的东西，于是英语会说某人的运气上升、下降或用完。

intro.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century from a Germanic source; its exact path is uncertain, but gambling gave it a firm place in everyday speech.
intro.cn: luck 于十五世纪从日耳曼语来源进入英语；确切路径不确定，但赌博让它在日常语言中站稳了脚。

items.en: Luck appears in written English in the fifteenth century as lucke, meaning good fortune.
items.cn: luck 在十五世纪以 lucke 的形式出现在书面英语中，意为好运。

items.en: Most accounts link it to Middle Dutch luc or the related Low German gelucke, though the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 多数说法把它与中古荷兰语 luc 或相关的低地德语 gelucke 联系起来，但确切来源路径并不确定。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the word was common at dice and card tables, where fortune was visibly decided by chance.
items.cn: 十六世纪时这个词常用于骰子和牌桌，在那里运气明显由偶然决定。

items.en: From games it widened to any event that people believed chance had decided.
items.cn: 它从游戏扩展到人们认为由偶然决定的任何事情。

items.en: Modern English uses luck for chance as a force, for good fortune, and for success that came without skill.
items.cn: 现代英语用 luck 指作为力量的偶然、好运气，以及不靠技巧而得来的成功。

note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示偶然以及命运所带来之物的词。

entries.definition: The power believed to fix what will happen to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为决定一个人遭遇的力量；命运。

entries.definition: A person's future seen as already settled.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为早已定下的人生归宿。

entries.definition: Bad luck or an unlucky event.

normalIntro.en: The word is short and its origin uncertain, so the hooks come from its family, its fixed phrases and its long association with games of chance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，来源又不确定，所以记忆钩子来自它的词族、固定短语，以及它与碰运气游戏的长期联系。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective simply means full of luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词的意思就是「带着运气的」。

normal.en: Luckily changes the y of lucky to i before adding -ly.
normal.cn: luckily 是先把 lucky 的 y 变成 i，再加 -ly。

normal.en: Luckless adds -less, the suffix of absence, so it means without luck.
normal.cn: luckless 加的是表示「没有」的后缀 -less，因此意为没有运气。

normal.en: By luck is a fixed phrase for something that happened through chance rather than plan.
normal.cn: by luck 是固定短语，指事情靠偶然而非计划发生。

normal.en: Luck out is informal and means to succeed by chance, keeping the old gambling flavour.
normal.cn: luck out 是口语说法，意为碰巧成功，保留了旧日赌博的意味。

abstract.en: A word for an unexplained cause becomes a word for a personal possession, because people would rather own fortune than admit they cannot explain it.
abstract.cn: 一个指无法解释之原因的词，变成了指个人所有物的词，因为人宁愿把运气归为己有，也不愿承认自己解释不了。

abstract.en: Luck sits between chance and fate: less planned than fate, more personal than pure chance.
abstract.cn: luck 处在偶然与命运之间：比命运更少安排，比纯粹的偶然更带个人色彩。

abstract.en: Every wish of good luck admits the same thing: the outcome is not fully in our hands.
abstract.cn: 每一句祝好运都承认同一件事：结果并不完全掌握在我们手里。

examples.cn: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。

examples.en: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
examples.cn: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。

scene: 雨刚停，一个赶路的人随手招了一下，空荡荡的街口竟真的停下一辆出租车。 He felt lucky as the taxi pulled up beside him.
sceneCN: 这里 lucky 是「幸运的、走运的」（第 1 个义项：本人有好运）；句意为出租车在他身边停下时，他感到自己很走运。画面里可认出雨后的街口与停下的出租车。

senses.title: Having good fortune in a particular situation
senses.definition: enjoying good fortune, especially when something good happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 享有好运，尤指好事偶然落到自己头上
senses.example: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。
senses.why: The noun luck names the force, and the suffix -y turns it into a quality, so a person can be described as having that force on their side.
senses.whyCN: 名词 luck 指这种力量，后缀 -y 把它变成一种性质，于是可以说一个人身上带着这种力量。

senses.title: Believed to bring good fortune to its owner
senses.definition: thought to bring good fortune to the person who has it or carries it
senses.definitionCN: 被认为能给拥有者或携带者带来好运的
senses.example: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。
senses.why: If a person can be lucky, then an object can be trusted to carry that luck, so the word spreads from people to charms and clothes.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以走运，人们也会相信某件物品能承载这份运气，于是词义从人扩展到护身符和衣物。

senses.title: Happening by chance in a favourable way
senses.definition: favourable but produced by accident rather than by skill or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 结果有利，却出自偶然而非技巧或知识
senses.example: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。
senses.why: When a good result arrives without skill, English calls it lucky, because the outcome is credited to fortune rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当好结果并非来自技巧时，英语称其为 lucky，因为这个结果被归功于运气而不是归功于人。

senses.title: Considered auspicious for a particular purpose
senses.definition: believed to be a favourable time, number or sign for something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为对某件事有利的时间、数字或征兆
senses.example: They chose the date because it was a lucky day in the old calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选这个日期，是因为它在旧历里是幸运日。
senses.why: From charms the word extends to days, numbers and signs, because people look for fortune not only in objects but also in timing.
senses.whyCN: 从护身符出发，这个词又扩展到日子、数字与征兆，因为人们不只在物件里找运气，也在时机里找。

intro.en: Lucky is the noun luck with the adjective suffix -y; the noun itself came into English from a Germanic source whose exact path is uncertain.
intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加形容词后缀 -y；这个名词本身来自日耳曼语来源，确切路径不确定。

items.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century, and the adjective lucky follows by adding -y to the noun.
items.cn: luck 于十五世纪进入英语，形容词 lucky 由名词加 -y 随后产生。

items.en: The noun is generally linked to Middle Dutch luc or Low German gelucke, though the exact source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，确切来源仍不确定。

items.en: Lucky appears in the sixteenth century, first around games of chance and then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: lucky 在十六世纪出现，最初用于碰运气的游戏，后来进入日常语言。

items.en: The suffix -y turns nouns into adjectives, as it does in health to healthy and luck to lucky.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，health 变 healthy、luck 变 lucky 都是这样。

items.en: Modern English uses lucky for people, charms, guesses, breaks and auspicious days.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lucky 形容人、护身符、猜测、好机会与吉日。

normal.en: Lucky break and lucky charm are fixed phrases, one for a chance opportunity and one for a trusted object.
normal.cn: lucky break 与 lucky charm 是固定短语，一个指偶然得来的机会，一个指被信赖的物件。

abstract.en: Calling a shirt lucky shows how easily people move fortune out of the body and into an object they can control.
abstract.cn: 把一件衬衫说成幸运，说明人很容易把运气从身体转移到一件自己能控制的物品上。

abstract.en: A lucky guess is praised and distrusted at once, because we want the result but not the randomness behind it.
abstract.cn: 侥幸猜中同时得到赞许与怀疑，因为我们想要结果，却不喜欢结果背后的偶然。

abstract.en: A lucky day is a way of making time itself take sides with a plan.
abstract.cn: 吉日是一种让时间本身站在计划一边的说法。
