items.exampleCN: 他们躲过风暴，真是幸运。

items.example: This year has been luckier than the last.
That was the luckiest day of his life.
items.exampleCN: 那是他一生中最幸运的一天。

items.example: Some actors think the play is unlucky.
items.exampleCN: 有些演员认为这部剧不吉利。

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：由名词构成形容词

definition_zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的；差得远的
definition_en: measuring a large distance from one side to the other, and figuratively covering a large range
core_image: 一条从田埂这头一直铺到那头的大河，两岸之间没有桥，只有很宽很宽的河面
scene: 站在河堤上，对岸的树像一条细线，中间的水面宽得望不到边。 The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
sceneCN: 这里 wide 是「宽的」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边距离大）；句意为河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。那条铺满整个视野、中间没有桥的河面，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的

senses.title: Large from side to side
senses.definition: measuring a good distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一边到另一边有相当长的距离
senses.example: The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。
senses.why: This physical span is the oldest and most literal sense, and every other use grows from it.
senses.whyCN: 这种物理上的跨度是最古老、最字面的意思，其他用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: Covering a large range
senses.definition: including many different things, kinds or people
senses.definitionCN: 包括许多不同的事物、种类或人
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of tools and paints.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类广泛的工具和油漆。
senses.why: A wide spread covers much ground, and a list of many kinds spreads in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的摊开占据大片地面，而涵盖许多种类的清单也是以同样方式铺开的。

senses.title: Fully open
senses.definition: used of eyes or doors that are opened to the full
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛或门被完全打开
senses.example: She stared at the letter with wide eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她睁大眼睛盯着那封信。
senses.why: A fully opened eye is stretched from side to side, so the measurement becomes a state of opening.
senses.whyCN: 完全睁开的眼睛两边拉长，于是这种度量变成了一种打开的状态。

senses.title: Far from the target
senses.definition: used of an answer or a shot that misses by a large distance
senses.definitionCN: 形容答案或射击偏离目标很远
senses.example: His guess was wide of the mark and made everyone laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他猜得完全不对，把大家都逗笑了。
senses.why: An arrow landing wide of the target is simply far across the field, and the image carried over to answers.
senses.whyCN: 箭落在靶子旁边的宽处，不过是横过大片场地，这一形象又被带到了答案上。

senses.title: Completely, in adverb use
senses.definition: as an adverb, used with open or apart to mean to the full extent
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时与 open、apart 搭配，表示达到最大限度
senses.example: The windows stood wide open all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午窗子都大开着。
senses.why: The adjective took the adverb job because English wants a word that measures the full opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词承担了副词的工作，因为英语需要一个词来衡量完全打开的程度。

intro.en: Wide comes from Old English wid, from a Germanic root that also gives width, and its first meaning was simply broad.
intro.cn: wide 源自古英语 wid，其日耳曼语词根也给出 width，最初的意思就是「宽阔」。

items.en: The root described something spread out across space, as opposed to long from end to end.
items.cn: 这个词根描述的是一样东西在空间中横向铺开，与「从头到尾的长」相对。

items.en: Wid meant broad and spacious, and the noun widu was already forming beside it.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔、空旷，旁边已经出现了名词形式。

items.en: The spelling became wide, and the word began to describe range as well as width.
items.cn: 拼写变为 wide，这个词除了宽度也开始描述范围。

items.en: Expressions such as a wide range and wide open extended it from the physical to the abstract.
items.cn: a wide range、wide open 这类说法把它从物理延伸到抽象。

items.en: The adverb use survives mainly in set pairs such as wide open, wide apart and far and wide.
items.cn: 副词用法主要保存在 wide open、wide apart、far and wide 等固定搭配中。

note.en: The first group gathers the other words of measurement, the second the words for a large range or spread.
note.cn: 第一组收其他度量词，第二组收表示范围大、分布广的词。

entries.definition: The measurement itself, from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 宽度

entries.definition: To make or become wide.
entries.definitionCN: 加宽；变宽

entries.definition: Living free in nature, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 野生的

entries.definition: Measuring a large distance end to end, the other axis.
entries.definitionCN: 长的

entries.definition: Wide, often of shoulders, roads or views.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的；开阔的

entries.definition: Covering a large area or range.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛的

entries.definition: Extremely wide, almost beyond measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 广阔的；巨大的

normalIntro.en: Wide is a measurement word, so picture something you could run across rather than turn end for end.
normalIntro.cn: wide 是度量词，所以要想象一样能横着跑过去的东西，而不是把它转一整圈。

normal.en: Wide and long are two axes; a door is wide, and a corridor is long.
normal.cn: wide 与 long 是两条轴：门是宽的，走廊是长的。

normal.en: Wide eyes and wide open share one picture of stretching to the limit.
normal.cn: wide eyes 与 wide open 共用一幅拉到极限的画面。

normal.en: A wide range is the same stretch, filled with kinds instead of metres.
normal.cn: a wide range 是同一种铺开，只是填的不是米，而是种类。

normal.en: Width turns the adjective into a noun by adding th.
normal.cn: width 加 th 就把形容词变成了名词。

normal.en: Far and wide means the span of the whole map.
normal.cn: far and wide 就是整张地图那么大的跨度。

abstract.en: Feel the wind crossing an open valley with nothing to stop it.
abstract.cn: 感觉风横穿开阔山谷，没有任何东西挡它。

abstract.en: See two banks so far apart that a voice would not carry.
abstract.cn: 看见两岸远到喊一声都传不过去。

abstract.en: Feel your eyes stretching at a surprising line.
abstract.cn: 感觉眼睛被一句意外的话撑开。

examples.en: The road is wide enough for two trucks to pass.
examples.cn: 这条路宽得能并排过两辆卡车。

examples.en: The museum offers a wide choice of free tours.
examples.cn: 博物馆提供了种类丰富的免费导览。

examples.en: She left the door wide open behind her.
examples.cn: 她离开时把门大开着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外得」——外面得留出很宽的余地，所以是宽的。

root: 日耳曼语词根（横向铺开）→ 古英语 wid（宽阔）→ 中古英语 wide → 现代英语 wide；同族有 width、widen、widely、widespread。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with the physical span from side to side, spreads to a range of things, to eyes opened fully, to a shot missing by a distance, and finally to the adverbial fully.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从左右之间的物理跨度出发，扩展到事物的范围、睁大的眼睛、偏得很远的射击，最后成为表示「完全」的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river so broad that the far bank is only a thin line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条大河宽到对岸只剩一条细线。

branches.en: The river branch: two banks far apart.
branches.cn: 河流分支：两岸相距很远。

branches.en: The range branch: tools and paints of many kinds.
branches.cn: 范围分支：种类繁多的工具与油漆。

branches.en: The eyes branch: staring at a letter.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：盯着那封信。

branches.en: The miss branch: a guess wide of the mark.
branches.cn: 偏离分支：猜得完全不对。

branches.en: The adverb branch: windows wide open.
branches.cn: 副词分支：窗子大开着。

intro.en: Wide is a free Germanic adjective that builds the noun width, the verb widen and the adverbs widely and wide.
intro.cn: wide 是自由使用的日耳曼语形容词，可派生名词 width、动词 widen 以及副词 widely、wide。

latinIntro.en: The native word has no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words often used for breadth and range.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出常用来表达宽度与范围的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective and adverb.

items.meaning: in a way, over a range

items.example: The adverb keeps its old breadth.
items.exampleCN: 副词保留了旧日的宽度感。

items.example: The pair spreads the word in two directions.
items.exampleCN: 这一对词把跨度向两个方向拉开。

items.example: It comes from shooting at a mark.

latinEntries.example: It gives English latitude, first width then freedom.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出 latitude，先指宽度后指自由。

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地
definition_en: not quite, but very close to being true or to happening; also used before amounts to mean a little less than the figure
core_image: 车门在眼前缓缓合上，脚尖离踏板只差半步
scene: 雨刚停，站台上的人陆续散去，广播已经在报最后一班车。 I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
sceneCN: 这里是「几乎、差一点」（第 1 个义项：接近但未达到）；句意为电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、广播、湿地面、车门。

pos.zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地

derivatives.zh: nearly 的词根，义为「近的；接近的」
由 near 加 -ness 构成，义为「接近；临近」，与 nearly 同族

senses.title: Almost, but not completely
senses.definition: not quite true or not quite done, though very close to it
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近，但还没有完全达到或完成
senses.example: I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。
senses.why: Near began as a word for physical closeness, and the ending -ly first meant in a close manner; spoken English then stretched that short gap from space into degree, so a thing that is close to happening becomes nearly happening.
senses.whyCN: near 原本表示空间上的接近，词尾 -ly 最初意为「以接近的方式」；口语把这个小缝隙从空间拉到位次，于是「接近发生」的事就成了「几乎发生」。

senses.title: Very close to a stated amount or time
senses.titleCN: 将近；差不多（数量或时间）
senses.definition: used before figures and periods to say that the real amount is a little below the one named
senses.definitionCN: 放在数字与时间段之前，表示实际数量略低于所说的那个数
senses.example: Nearly a thousand people came to the opening.
senses.exampleCN: 将近一千人参加了开幕式。
senses.why: Measuring a short distance and measuring a small shortfall use the same picture, so the word that once said two places are close now says a total is close to a round figure.
senses.whyCN: 量一小段距离与量一小点差额用的是同一幅画面，于是那个原本说「两地相近」的词，现在说「总数接近某个整数」。

senses.title: Closely, in family connections
senses.titleCN: 密切地；亲近地（指亲属关系）
senses.definition: used with related or connected to mean closely, chiefly in older or careful English
senses.definitionCN: 与 related 等词连用表示「关系密切」，多见于较旧或较正式的英语
senses.example: The two families were nearly related by marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个家庭因婚姻而关系很近。
senses.why: The older sense of the adverb was simply closely, and kinship is where that sense survives; the everyday sense moved away to almost, leaving this use behind like a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词较早的意思就是「紧密地」，亲属关系正是这层意思的留存处；日常义漂向「几乎」，把这一用法像化石一样留在了原地。

intro.en: Nearly is near plus the old adverb ending, and its meaning drifted from closely to almost while one formal use kept the older sense.
intro.cn: nearly 是 near 加旧副词词尾，词义从「紧密地」漂到「几乎」，只有一种正式用法保留了旧义。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative gave English the form near that nearly is built on.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级给英语提供了 near 这个形式，nearly 就建在它上面。

items.en: The ending -lice meant in the manner of, and it is the ancestor of the modern -ly in nearly and other adverbs.
items.cn: -lice 意为「以……的方式」，是现代副词词尾 -ly 的前身，nearly 等词都用它。

items.en: Middle English ner meant both near and closely, and the new adverb nerliche carried the sense of closely, carefully.
items.cn: 中古英语 ner 兼有「近」与「紧密」两义，新的副词 nerliche 表示「紧密地、仔细地」。

items.en: The adverb is recorded in the sixteenth century; by the seventeenth the sense almost is common in speech and in print.
items.cn: 这个副词在十六世纪见于记录；到十七世纪，「几乎」义已在口语与书面语中常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps almost as the main sense, adds the counting use before numbers, and retains closely only in phrases about kinship.
items.cn: 现代英语以「几乎」为主义，又添上数字前的计量用法，只在与亲属关系有关的短语里保留「密切地」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the root and the forms built directly on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs that stop just short of a fact.
note.cn: 形近组收词根以及直接建在词根上的形式；近义组收其他表示「差一点、差不多」的副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, in space, time or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 空间、时间或程度上不远的。

entries.definition: The quality of being close, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的「接近、临近」这一性质。

entries.definition: The comparative of near, for a smaller distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的比较级，表示更近的距离。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the smallest distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示最近的距离。

entries.definition: Very close to, and often interchangeable with nearly before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 非常接近，在动词前常可与 nearly 互换。

entries.definition: In effect, though not strictly true; stronger in speech than nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上差不多，口语中语气比 nearly 更强。

entries.definition: Almost entirely, used of conditions rather than of counted things.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎完全，多用于状态而非可数之物。

entries.definition: About, allowing for a margin on either side rather than falling short.
entries.definitionCN: 大约，允许上下浮动，而不专指不足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic root for closeness with an old adverb ending, and its main sense has slid from manner into degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语「接近」词根加旧副词词尾，主义从「方式」滑到了「程度」。

normal.en: Near means close, and -ly once meant in that manner, so nearly first described how something was done, not how complete it was.
normal.cn: near 意为近，-ly 原表示「以那种方式」，所以 nearly 最初描述的是做法，而不是完成程度。

normal.en: Before a verb, nearly and almost usually exchange freely: I nearly fell, I almost fell.
normal.cn: 在动词前，nearly 与 almost 通常可以互换：I nearly fell 与 I almost fell 意思相同。

normal.en: Before a number, nearly means a little below it; about or approximately allows the figure to be above as well.
normal.cn: 在数字前，nearly 表示略低于该数；about 或 approximately 则允许高于该数。

normal.en: Not nearly is a fixed phrase of strong denial: the job is not nearly finished means it is far from finished.
normal.cn: not nearly 是语气很强的固定说法：「the job is not nearly finished」意为「离完成还差得远」。

normal.en: Nearly related keeps the old sense of closely, which is why it sounds formal beside the everyday almost.
normal.cn: nearly related 保留了「密切」的旧义，所以它放在日常的 almost 旁边会显得正式。

abstract.en: A closing door measured in half steps shows how English turns a gap in space into a gap in degree.
abstract.cn: 用半步来量的合上的车门，说明英语怎样把空间里的缝隙变成程度上的缝隙。

abstract.en: The same word can fall just short of a train and just short of a thousand, because counting is only measuring with numbers.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以差一点赶上车，也可以差一点到一千，因为计数不过是拿数字来量。

abstract.en: A fossil sense survives in family talk, reminding us that nearly once meant tightly, not almost.
abstract.cn: 一个化石般的旧义活在亲属称谓里，提醒人 nearly 曾经意为「紧紧地」，而不是「几乎」。

examples.en: The bottle is nearly empty; we need another.
examples.cn: 瓶子快空了，我们得再拿一瓶。

examples.en: She has worked here for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在这里工作了将近二十年。

examples.en: It was nearly midnight when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响的时候已将近午夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔利」——差一步就到「near」，可惜还没到；nearly 就是几乎、差一点。

root: 古英语 neah（近）的比较级 near，加副词词尾 -lice（现代 -ly）构成；属日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small remaining gap; it can be a gap before an event, a gap below a number, or the old gap of close kinship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「剩下的一小段差距」；它可以是事件之前的差距、数字以下的差距，也可以是旧义里亲属之间的贴近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train door sliding shut while one foot is still half a step from the step.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门正在合上，一只脚离踏板还差半步。

branches.en: a hand reaching a door as it closes
branches.cn: 车门合上时伸过去的手

branches.en: a platform emptying after the last announcement
branches.cn: 最后一次广播后渐渐空去的站台

branches.en: a hall filled just short of a thousand
branches.cn: 坐得差一点满一千人的大厅

branches.en: a guest list counted twice at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上数了两遍的宾客名单

branches.en: two families joined by one marriage
branches.cn: 因一桩婚姻连在一起的两家人

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of closeness, an Old English adverb ending, and the modern shapes of both.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语表示「接近」的形容词、一个古英语副词词尾，以及两者在现代的形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Nearly belongs to the Germanic family of near, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: nearly 属于 near 这一日耳曼语词族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: all but, by a very small margin

definition_zh: 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；短暂的；急躁的；活着的
definition_en: moving or happening at great speed; able to think or notice fast; lasting only a short time; easily made angry; alive, in an old use
core_image: 一只掠过水面的蜻蜓，翅膀几乎看不清
scene: 清晨的厨房里，水壶刚响，她一边系围裙一边把面包推进烤槽。 A quick breakfast was all she had time for before the bus came.
sceneCN: 这里 quick 是「短暂的、匆匆的」（第 3 个义项：只持续很短时间）；句意为在公交车来之前，她只来得及吃一顿匆匆的早餐。画面里可留意：响了的水壶、半系的围裙、烤槽里的面包。

pos.zh: 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；短暂的；急躁的

derivatives.zh: quick 与 witted 复合，指脑筋转得快的

senses.title: Moving or happening fast
senses.definition: moving, acting or happening with high speed
senses.definitionCN: 以很高的速度移动、行动或发生
senses.example: She gave a quick reply and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她迅速回答了一句就离开了房间。
senses.why: Old English cwic meant alive, and lively movement is the first thing the word came to describe.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cwic 意为「活着的」，而活物最显眼的表现就是动作迅速，这是这个词最先用来描述的东西。

senses.title: Able to think or notice fast
senses.definition: able to understand or notice something in a very short time
senses.definitionCN: 能在极短时间内理解或察觉
senses.example: He has a quick mind for figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他对数字反应很快。
senses.why: A lively body and a lively mind were both described with the word for alive, so mental speed joined physical speed.
senses.whyCN: 活的身体与活的头脑都用「活着」这个词来描述，于是心智的敏捷也加入了身体的速度义。

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: taking or lasting only a little time
senses.definitionCN: 只花或只持续很少的时间
senses.example: We took a quick look at the map before we left.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前我们匆匆看了一眼地图。
senses.why: If an action is fast, it also ends soon, so the word came to describe anything brief rather than merely fast.
senses.whyCN: 一个动作既然快，也就会很快结束，于是这个词转而形容任何短暂之物，而不只是形容速度快。

senses.title: Easily made angry
senses.definition: tending to become angry very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 很容易突然发怒的
senses.example: He has a quick temper and regrets it at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他脾气急躁，发完火马上就后悔。
senses.why: A quick temper ignites fast, and the same adjective for speed was applied to the speed of anger rather than of motion.
senses.whyCN: 急性子发火快，于是这个表示速度的形容词被用到愤怒的速度上，而不是移动的速度上。

senses.title: Alive, in old use
senses.definition: living, in language that survives mainly in old texts and set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 活着的，主要保留在旧文本与固定说法中
senses.example: The old sermon spoke of the quick and the dead.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的布道讲到了生者与死者。
senses.why: Cwic meant alive in Old English, and this oldest sense now survives only in fixed phrases and in the saying the quick and the dead.
senses.whyCN: cwic 在古英语中就是「活着的」，这一最古老的意思如今只留在固定说法与 the quick and the dead 这句里。

intro.en: Quick is a native English word whose oldest meaning was alive; the sense of speed grew from the liveliness of living things.
intro.cn: quick 是英语本族词，最古老的意思是「活着的」；速度义是从活物的活跃状态生长出来的。

items.en: Cwic meant alive or living, and it described people, animals and even running water.
items.cn: cwic 意为活着的、有生命的，可形容人、动物，甚至流动的水。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic with the same sense of alive, and related forms appear in other northern languages.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为同样的「活着」义，其他北方语言中也有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English quick widened from alive to lively, and from lively to fast.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quick 从「活着」扩展到「活跃」，又从「活跃」扩展到「快」。

items.en: The speed sense became dominant, while the sense of alive retreated into set phrases such as the quick and the dead.
items.cn: 速度义成为主导，而「活着」义退入 the quick and the dead 这类固定说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the senses of a short duration, of a sharp mind and of a short temper.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了持续时间短、脑筋快、脾气急这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same old root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of speed and alertness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词根上的形式；近义组收表示速度与机敏的形容词。

entries.definition: At high speed.
entries.definitionCN: 以很快的速度。

entries.definition: To make or become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 使变快或变快。

entries.definition: The quality of being fast.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速、敏捷的性质。

entries.definition: Loose sand that swallows what stands on it.
entries.definitionCN: 会吞没立足之物的流沙，其中 quick 仍是「活的」旧义。

entries.definition: Moving or done at high speed.
entries.definitionCN: 高速移动或完成的。

entries.definition: Happening in a very short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在极短时间内发生的。

entries.definition: Moving smoothly and quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 平稳而迅速地移动的。

entries.definition: Done without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 毫不拖延地完成的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as alive, moved to lively, then to fast, and finally to brief; each step is shorter than the one before.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「活着」开始，走到「活跃」，再到「快」，最后到「短暂」；每一步都比上一步更短。

normal.en: Quick and quicksand share the old sense of alive: quicksand behaves like something living because it shifts and swallows.
normal.cn: quick 与 quicksand 共用旧义「活的」：流沙会移动、会吞没，行为像活物。

normal.en: Quickly is the adverb, quicken the verb, quickness the noun: three endings from one short root.
normal.cn: quickly 是副词，quicken 是动词，quickness 是名词：一个短词根带出三个词尾。

normal.en: A quick temper is a temper that ignites fast, not a temper that lasts long.
normal.cn: a quick temper 指点火快的脾气，不是持续久的脾气。

normal.en: The quick and the dead is the one common phrase where quick still means alive.
normal.cn: the quick and the dead 是 quick 仍然表示「活着的」的唯一常见说法。

normal.en: Quick to learn describes the speed of learning, while a quick study describes the person who learns fast.
normal.cn: quick to learn 描述学习的速度，而 a quick study 指学得快的人。

abstract.en: Speed began as a sign of life, and the modern word keeps that trace in phrases about the living.
abstract.cn: 速度最初是生命的标志，现代这个词仍在关于生者的说法里留着那道痕迹。

abstract.en: A quick answer can be a sign of a sharp mind or of a careless one, and the word alone cannot tell which.
abstract.cn: 迅速的回答既可能是脑筋敏锐，也可能是草率，光凭这个词分辨不出来。

abstract.en: To call someone quick is to praise a body and a mind at once, as if they moved on the same clock.
abstract.cn: 说一个人 quick，是同时称赞身体与头脑，仿佛它们走在同一只钟上。

examples.en: He took a quick shower and ran for the train.
examples.cn: 他匆匆冲了个澡就去赶火车。

examples.en: She is quick at catching small mistakes in a text.
examples.cn: 她很善于抓住文章里的小错误。

examples.en: Be careful with him; he has a quick temper.
examples.cn: 和他打交道要小心，他脾气很急。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快克」——快客一到，事情立刻办完，记住 quick 是快的、迅速的。

root: 古英语 cwic（活着的）→ 中古英语 quick（活跃的）→ 现代英语 quick（快的、短暂的）；同族有 quickly、quicken、quicksand。

sensesIntro.en: The core is liveliness; the senses move from being alive to moving fast, to thinking fast, to lasting briefly, to a fast temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「活跃」；义项从活着走向动作快，再到思维快、持续时间短，最后到脾气急。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dragonfly skimming the water, its wings almost too fast to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只掠过水面的蜻蜓，翅膀快得几乎看不清。

branches.en: a foot landing before the eye follows
branches.cn: 眼睛还没跟上，脚已经落地

branches.en: an answer given before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题还没问完就给出的回答

branches.en: a glance at a map at a bus stop
branches.cn: 在公交站匆匆看一眼地图

branches.en: a match struck and already burning
branches.cn: 火柴一划就已燃起

branches.en: the same speed, once admired and once feared
branches.cn: 同一种速度，一次被赞赏，一次被畏惧

intro.en: The word is native English and carries its meaning through a short root plus endings for adverbs, verbs and nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，靠一个短词根加上副词、动词与名词词尾来承载词义。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 在里面；内部；内侧
definition_en: the inner part or surface of something; located within
core_image: 盒盖合上后灯还亮着的那一小块空间
scene: 快递箱拆开时全家都围了上来。 The keys are inside the drawer.
sceneCN: 这里 inside 是「在里面」（第 1 个义项：处于内部）；句意：钥匙在抽屉里面。

derivatives.zh: inside 加施动者后缀，义为「内部人士」
inside 的复数，义为「内脏；内部构造」

senses.title: The inner part of a thing
senses.definition: the inner part or surface of something
senses.definitionCN: 物体的内部或内表面
senses.example: The inside of the bag is lined with silk.
senses.exampleCN: 包的内衬是丝绸。
senses.why: Open the lid and the lamp space appears.
senses.whyCN: 掀开盖子，那片亮着的小空间出现。

senses.title: Within a place or thing
senses.definition: located or moving within something
senses.definitionCN: 位于或进入某物之内
senses.example: The cat hid inside the wardrobe.
senses.exampleCN: 猫藏在衣柜里。
senses.why: The lid closes and the space holds its guest.
senses.whyCN: 盖子合上，小空间收留了客人。

senses.title: Inner-facing position
senses.definition: facing or belonging to the inner side
senses.definitionCN: 朝向或属于内侧
senses.example: Keep the map in your inside pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 把地图放进内袋。
senses.why: The pocket sewn toward the lamp space.
senses.whyCN: 缝向那片小空间的口袋。

senses.title: Secret, known to a few
senses.definition: known only to people within a group
senses.definitionCN: 只有圈内人知晓
senses.example: He traded on inside information.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用内幕消息交易。
senses.why: Only those under the lid can see the lamp.
senses.whyCN: 只有盖子下的人看得见灯。

senses.title: Into the interior
senses.definition: moving toward the inner part
senses.definitionCN: 向内部移动
senses.example: They went inside when it snowed.
senses.exampleCN: 下雪时他们走进了屋里。
senses.why: One step across the lid line.
senses.whyCN: 跨过盖线的一步。

intro.en: Inside is in + side, formed inside English. The picture is simply the side that faces inward.
intro.cn: inside 由 in + side 在英语内部合成，画面就是朝向内侧的那一面。

items.en: Old English side meant the flank or edge of a body.
items.cn: 古英语 side 指身体的侧边或边缘。

items.en: Phrases like inside of a house named the inner flank.
items.cn: 短语 inside of a house 指屋子的内侧。

items.en: The compound fused into one word for all positions.
items.cn: 复合词融为一体，用于各种位置。

items.en: Modern English spread it to time (inside a week) and secrets.
items.cn: 现代英语将其扩展到时间（一周之内）与内幕。

items.en: Insider was coined for the person who stands under the lid.
items.cn: insider 一词被造出来，指站在盖子下的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the side family. The meaning group compares words of being within.
note.cn: 形近组收录 side 词族；词义组比较表示「在内」的词。

entries.definition: the direct antonym.
entries.definitionCN: 直接反义词。

entries.definition: a member who knows secrets.
entries.definitionCN: 知晓内情的内部人士。

entries.definition: the inner parts or organs.
entries.definitionCN: 内部；内脏。

entries.definition: inside a range or boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 在范围之内。

entries.definition: the inner region.
entries.definitionCN: 内部区域。

entries.definition: inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑物内。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the inner side image, the pocket pair and the secret use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用内侧面意象、内袋配对与内幕用法。

normal.en: in plus side: the side that faces inward.
normal.cn: in 加 side：朝内的一面。

normal.en: an inside pocket faces your body.
normal.cn: an inside pocket 贴着身体。

normal.en: inside information is for under-the-lid ears.
normal.cn: inside information 是盖子下的耳语。

normal.en: insides means your inner parts.
normal.cn: insides 指体内器官。

normal.en: outside is the mirror twin.
normal.cn: outside 是镜子里的孪生词。

abstract.en: One image: a lit space after the lid clicks shut.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：盖子咔哒合上后仍亮着的小空间。

abstract.en: Inside is where the lamp keeps burning unseen.
abstract.cn: inside 是灯在无人处仍亮着的地方。

abstract.en: Every box keeps a warm heart.
abstract.cn: 每个盒子都藏着一颗温暖的心。

examples.en: There is a label inside the jacket.
examples.cn: 夹克内侧有一张标签。

examples.en: She knows the industry from the inside.
examples.cn: 她从内部了解这个行业。

examples.en: The parcel was damaged on the inside.
examples.cn: 包裹内部受损了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因塞德」：因藏于内，塞得深德（得）稳， inside。

root: 古英语 side「侧边」→ 中古英语短语 inside of「……的内侧」→ 复合为介词、名词、形容词、副词 inside → 现代英语扩展出内幕义；反义 outside。

sensesIntro.en: Inside is the inward side: the lit space under a lid, the pocket turned to the body, the secret kept under it, and the step across the line.
sensesIntro.cn: inside 是朝内的一面：盖下亮着的空间、贴身的口袋、盖下保守的秘密，以及跨线的那一步。

core.en: The side that faces inward and keeps what the lid closes in.
core.cn: 朝向内侧、在盖合之后收藏一切的那一面。

branches.en: INTERIOR: lined with silk inside.
branches.cn: 内部：内衬丝绸。

branches.en: ENCLOSURE: hid inside the wardrobe.
branches.cn: enclosure：藏进衣柜。

branches.en: PROXIMITY: the inside pocket.
branches.cn: 贴身：内袋。

branches.en: SECRECY: inside information.
branches.cn: 内幕：内部消息。

branches.en: ENTRY: they went inside.
branches.cn: 进入：他们走进屋内。

intro.en: Inside builds insider, insides and its mirror outside.
intro.cn: inside 构成 insider、insides 及镜面词 outside。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries: this compound is pure English.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁条目：该复合词是纯正英语造词。

items.example: The insides of the clock were clean.
A lamp stood beside the bed.

definition_zh: 戒指；环形物；铃声；给……打电话；响铃
definition_en: a circle of metal worn as jewelry, a circular shape, a sound of a bell, or to call someone by phone
core_image: 一圈首尾相接的圆环：戴在手上是戒指，敲响是铃声，接通是电话
scene: 生日那天他送给她一枚戒指，她高兴得直笑。 He gave her a beautiful ring for her birthday, and she smiled with joy.
sceneCN: 这里 ring 是「戒指」（第 1 个义项：戴在手上的环形首饰）；句意：生日那天他送给她一枚漂亮的戒指，她笑得很开心。

pos.zh: 响铃；按铃；打电话；成环形

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 后缀构成，指按铃的人或声音极像的人
由现在分词转形容词，义为「响亮的；响个不停的」
由 ear 加 ring 构成的合成词，义为「耳环」

senses.title: A band of jewelry
senses.definition: a piece of jewelry shaped like a circle that you wear on your finger
senses.definitionCN: 戴在手指上的环形首饰
senses.example: She wears a gold ring on her finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她手指上戴着一枚金戒指。
senses.why: The circle shape of metal around a finger is the oldest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 金属围成一个圈戴在手上，是这个词最古老、最直观的画面。

senses.title: A circular shape
senses.definition: any object or area shaped like a circle
senses.definitionCN: 任何圆形的物体或区域
senses.example: The children danced in a ring.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们围成一圈跳舞。
senses.why: The shape itself extends beyond jewelry to anything round and closed.
senses.whyCN: 圆环的形状从首饰延伸到一切首尾相接的圆形物体或区域。

senses.title: A ringing sound
senses.definition: the sound made by a bell or a phone
senses.definitionCN: 铃或电话发出的声音
senses.example: There was a ring at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃响了。
senses.why: A bell is shaped like a ring, and its repeated sound became the name of the sound.
senses.whyCN: 钟铃形似圆环，其反复震响的声音也被借用来指铃声本身。

senses.title: To make a bell sound
senses.definition: to cause a bell to make a sound
senses.definitionCN: 使铃发出声音
senses.example: Someone is ringing the doorbell.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在按门铃。
senses.why: Once the sound is named, the action that produces it takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 声音有了名字，发出这种声音的动作也顺理成章地用同一个词。

senses.title: To call by phone
senses.definition: to telephone someone, especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 给某人打电话，英式英语常用
senses.example: I will ring you tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我今晚给你打电话。
senses.why: Early telephones rang a bell when called, so the bell action transferred to phone calls.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话靠摇铃呼叫，铃的动作自然转移到打电话这件事上。

intro.en: Ring comes from Old English hring, meaning a circle or something bent into a loop.
intro.cn: ring 源自古英语 hring，意为圆环或弯成圈状之物。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root *hringaz means a circle or curved band.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语词根 *hringaz 意为圆圈或弯曲的环带，一般认为这是该词的共同源头。

items.en: Hring in Old English already meant both a circular band and jewelry.
items.cn: 古英语 hring 已兼指环形物与环形首饰，戒指义从一开始就存在。

items.en: The verb sense of making a bell sound appears from the sound of struck metal.
items.cn: 动词「鸣响」义来自敲击金属时绕梁的余音，与铃声的反复回荡相关，属拟声性引申。

items.en: Ring keeps the circle senses and gains the bell sense.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 ring 保留圆环各义项，并固定下钟铃响声义。

items.en: The telephone brings a new use: to ring someone up means to call them.
items.cn: 电话机发明后，ring 的新用法诞生：ring someone up 即给某人打电话。

items.en: British English keeps ring for phone calls, while American English prefers call.
items.cn: 英式英语沿用 ring 表示打电话，美式英语更常用 call，形成今天的地区差异。

note.en: Ring has look-alike words about circles and near-meaning words about sounds and calls.
note.cn: ring 的形近词多与圆形相关，近义词则集中在声音与打电话的义场。

entries.definition: a small ring-shaped curl of hair
entries.definitionCN: 小卷发；小环，由 ring 加指小后缀构成，与 ring 同源

entries.definition: a floor for ice skating
entries.definitionCN: 溜冰场，拼写相近且读音略同，但词源与圆环无关，只是形近

entries.definition: to twist and squeeze something
entries.definitionCN: 拧；绞，读音与 ring 完全相同但拼写多一个 w，词源不同，需靠语境区分

entries.definition: a perfectly round shape or a group arranged in a round form
entries.definitionCN: 圆；圈子，泛指圆形与围成的圈，不特指首饰

entries.definition: to telephone someone
entries.definitionCN: 打电话，美式英语的常用说法，与英式 ring 相对

entries.definition: to make a clear ringing sound like a bell
entries.definitionCN: 鸣响；敲出清脆的钟声，强调悦耳的乐音而非铃的动作

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember ring through its shape and sound.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕圆环形状与铃声的记忆路径。

normal.en: RING has a circular G at the end, like the ring itself closing into a loop.
normal.cn: RING 结尾的 G 圆圆的，就像戒指首尾相接的小圆环。

normal.en: A wedding ring goes on the r-ight f-inger: R + ING.
normal.cn: 婚戒戴在「right（右手）」的手指上：R 加 ING 就是戒指。

normal.en: The phone RINGS: ring-ring is the sound itself, so the word imitates the bell.
normal.cn: 电话铃「ring-ring」响，这个拟声式的叠音就是铃声本身。

normal.en: EAR + RING = earring, the same circle moved to the ear.
normal.cn: 耳朵加圆环就是耳环 earring，同一只圆环换了个位置。

normal.en: Boxing RING is a square but the fighters are enclosed in a circle of ropes.
normal.cn: 拳击台叫 ring，虽然台子是方的，但四周被围绳圈住，保留了「围成圈」的古义。

abstract.en: Imagine a golden circle floating in the air, waiting to be worn.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金色圆环悬浮空中，等待有人把它戴上。

abstract.en: Hear the bell echo in circles, each sound wave a smaller ring.
abstract.cn: 听钟声一圈圈荡开，每一道声波都是一枚缩小的小圆环。

abstract.en: A phone call draws a ring that connects two people across distance.
abstract.cn: 一通电话画出一道圆环，把相隔两地的两个人连在一起。

examples.en: He slipped the ring onto her finger.
examples.cn: 他把戒指轻轻套上她的手指。

examples.en: Please ring me when you arrive at the station.
examples.cn: 你到车站后请给我打电话。

examples.en: The church bells ring every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 教堂的钟每星期天早晨都会敲响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锐赢」——戴着亮闪闪的戒指去比赛，锐气逼人，赢面大增；ring 读音近似「锐赢」

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语词根 *hringaz（圆环、弯曲的环带），古英语 hring 直承此义；动词鸣响义属拟声性引申，与圆环名词同形但来源路径不同。

sensesIntro.en: Ring moves from a circular band of metal to any circle, then to bell sounds and phone calls.
sensesIntro.cn: ring 从金属圆环出发，扩展到一切圈状物，再引申出铃声与打电话等义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed circle of metal
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚首尾相接的金属圆环

branches.en: The circle shape covers both finger jewelry and any round arrangement.

branches.en: The repeated clang of a bell becomes the name of the sound.
branches.cn: 钟铃反复的敲击声被用作声音本身的名称。

branches.en: The action of making a bell sound takes the same word.
branches.cn: 使铃发声的动作沿用同一个词。

branches.en: Early telephones rang bells, so calling someone became ringing them.
branches.cn: 早期电话靠铃声呼叫，打电话由此借用了响铃的说法。

branches.en: Jewelry and bells share the metal circle: same shape, different use.
branches.cn: 首饰与钟铃共享金属圆环这一形状：同形而用途不同。

intro.en: Ring forms compounds and derivatives around its circle shape and bell sound.
intro.cn: ring 的构词围绕圆环形状与铃声两条线索展开。

definition_zh: 原因；理由；理性；道理；推理；说服
definition_en: a cause or justification for something; the power of logical thought; good sense or fairness; to think logically; to persuade someone by argument
core_image: 白板上一条从问题连到答案的清晰线
scene: 白板上，一条线从问题连到答案，每一步都标得清楚。 There is no reason to doubt her story.
sceneCN: 这里 reason 是「理由」（第 1 个义项：支持某判断的根据）；句意为没有理由怀疑她的说法。画面里可留意：白板上连到答案的线、标清楚的每一步。

derivatives.zh: reason 加 -able，指合理的、公道的
reason 加 -ed，指经过推理的、有条理的

senses.title: A cause or justification
senses.definition: a cause or explanation that justifies something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供根据的原因或解释
senses.example: There is no reason to doubt her story.
senses.exampleCN: 没有理由怀疑她的说法。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reason is the reckoning that stands behind a claim or an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而理由就是支撑一个说法或事件的那笔「计算」。

senses.title: The power of logical thought
senses.definition: the human power of thinking logically and drawing conclusions
senses.definitionCN: 进行逻辑思考并得出结论的心智能力
senses.example: Reason separates a careful judge from a rash one.
senses.exampleCN: 理性把谨慎的判断者与草率者区分开来。
senses.why: The same reckoning that gives a reason for a claim is also the faculty that performs the reckoning, so reason names the mind's calculating power.
senses.whyCN: 支撑说法的计算，也是完成计算的能力，因此 reason 指心智的计算力。

senses.title: Good sense or fairness
senses.definition: good sense, fairness or what is right in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 良好判断、公平，或处境中正确之事
senses.example: There is reason in what she says, even if we disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话里有道理，即使我们不同意。
senses.why: What follows reason is felt as right and fair, so the word came to name the quality of being in accordance with good sense.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之事被感受为正确而公平，于是这个词也命名「合乎常理」的品质。

senses.title: To think logically
senses.definition: to think through facts and form a judgment by logic
senses.definitionCN: 梳理事实并用逻辑形成判断
senses.example: He reasoned that the letter must have been sent yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 他推断这封信一定是昨天寄出的。
senses.why: Reason as a verb is simply the mind doing what the noun names: reckoning from facts toward a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 作动词的 reason 就是心智做名词所指之事：从事实推算到结论。

senses.title: To persuade by argument
senses.definition: to persuade someone by presenting arguments rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过提出论据而非强力来说服某人
senses.example: She tried to reason with the angry customer.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着与愤怒的顾客讲道理。
senses.why: When reasoning is aimed at another person, the verb means to bring that person's mind into line through argument.
senses.whyCN: 当推理指向另一个人时，这个动词便指通过论证把对方的心拉到同一线上。

intro.en: Reason comes from Old French reisun, from Latin ratio, reckoning and reason, which itself comes from reri, to reckon or think.
intro.cn: reason 来自古法语 reisun，源于拉丁语 ratio（计算与理性），而 ratio 又来自 reri（计算、思考）。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon or think, the act behind every form of this family.
items.cn: reri 意为计算或思考，是整个词族背后的动作。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning and also the faculty of reason that makes reckoning possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算，也指使计算成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: Old French reisun carried the word to English with the sense of a cause and of good judgment.
items.cn: 古法语 reisun 把这个词带到英语，带着「原因」与「良好判断」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reason kept both the explanation and the thinking power, and added the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 reason 既保留解释，也保留思维能力，并加上了动词用法。

items.en: Modern English uses reason for causes, for the thinking power, for fairness, for logical argument, and for persuading.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reason 指原因、思维能力、公平、逻辑论证，以及说服。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same reckoning root; the near-meaning group gathers words for cause, logic and persuasion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「计算」词根的词；近义组收表示原因、逻辑与说服的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is reckoning: it names the cause behind an event, the mind that reckons, the fairness that reckoning yields, and the acts of reasoning and persuading.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「计算」：它命名事件背后的原因、进行计算的心智、计算带来的公平，以及推理与说服的行为。

normal.en: Reason and ratio come from the same Latin word for reckoning.
normal.cn: reason 与 ratio 来自同一个表示「计算」的拉丁词。

normal.en: The reason for a thing is the explanation that stands behind it.
normal.cn: 一物的 reason，就是站在它背后的解释。

normal.en: Reason as a power is what lets a person follow an argument.
normal.cn: 作为能力的 reason，使人能够跟上论证。

normal.en: Within reason means inside the limits of what makes sense.
normal.cn: within reason 意为在合乎情理的限度之内。

normal.en: To reason with someone is to argue calmly rather than force them.
normal.cn: to reason with 某人，是平静论理而非强迫对方。

abstract.en: A reason is a bridge between a fact and a conclusion.
abstract.cn: reason 是事实与结论之间的一座桥。

abstract.en: Reason can be used to justify almost anything, which is why it needs honesty.
abstract.cn: 理性几乎可以为任何事辩护，因此它需要诚实。

abstract.en: To lose one's reason is to lose the bridge, not the world.
abstract.cn: 失去理智，是失去那座桥，而不是失去世界。

definition_zh: 谋杀；凶杀；谋杀罪；糟蹋；彻底击败
definition_en: the crime of killing a person deliberately; to kill someone unlawfully and on purpose; also, in loose use, to ruin a piece of work or defeat an opponent completely
core_image: 一只手的影子按在另一个人的影子上，把对方从地面上抹去
scene: 侦探在雨后的巷口拉起警戒线，墙角的脚印还湿着，围观的人低声说这不像意外。 The detective read the report and concluded that the man had been murdered in his own kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「谋杀、蓄意杀害」（第 1 个义项：非法且故意地夺去他人性命）；句意为侦探看过报告后断定这名男子是在自家厨房里被杀害的。图中可辨识物件：警戒线、湿脚印、厨房门。

pos.zh: 蓄意杀害；糟蹋；彻底击败

derivatives.zh: 由 murder 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「凶手；谋杀者」
由 murder 加 -ous 构成，义为「蓄意杀人的；极其危险的」
由 murderer 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女凶手」

senses.title: The crime of killing a person on purpose
senses.definition: the crime of killing another person deliberately and unlawfully
senses.definitionCN: 非法且故意地杀害他人的罪行
senses.example: The trial lasted two weeks and ended in a verdict of murder.
senses.exampleCN: 审判持续了两周，最终裁定为谋杀。
senses.why: Old English morthor named a hidden killing, a death kept secret, so the word first recorded concealment rather than the weapon.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 morthor 指暗中进行的杀害，是「不让外人知道的死亡」，所以这个词最早记录的重点是隐秘，而不是凶器。

senses.title: To kill a person unlawfully and deliberately
senses.definition: to kill someone on purpose and against the law
senses.definitionCN: 故意且违法地夺去他人生命
senses.example: Police believe the same person murdered two shopkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 警方认为同一个人杀害了两名店主。
senses.why: Once the noun named the hidden act, the verb could name doing it, and the law uses the pair to separate a planned killing from an accident.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这种隐秘的行为，动词就能指做出这种行为；法律用这一对词把有预谋的杀害与意外区分开。

senses.title: Murder as a charge in law
senses.definition: the offence itself as charged in court, carrying the heaviest penalty in many legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上被指控的罪名本身，在许多法律体系里对应最重的刑罚
senses.example: He was charged with murder and held without bail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控谋杀，不得保释。
senses.why: Legal language turned the act into a countable charge, so murder can stand in a courtroom list beside theft and fraud.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把这种行为变成一个可列举的罪名，于是 murder 能和盗窃、欺诈一起出现在法庭的罪名清单里。

senses.title: To ruin a performance or defeat an opponent badly
senses.definition: in informal use, to spoil a piece of work or beat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中把作品弄坏，或以很大差距击败对手
senses.example: The young pianist murdered the difficult passage but never lost the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻钢琴手把那一段难弹的乐句糟蹋了，却始终没有失去听众。
senses.why: The violent core image survives in slang as exaggeration: a singer who murders a song figuratively kills it, and the same hyperbole covers a heavy defeat.
senses.whyCN: 暴力的核心意象在俚语里以夸张的方式保留下来：歌手 murder 一首歌，就是把歌「弄死」了；同样的夸张也用来形容惨败。

intro.en: Murder is one of the oldest English words for killing, and its earliest use stresses secrecy rather than the manner of death.
intro.cn: murder 是英语里最古老的表示杀害的词之一，最早的用法强调的是隐秘，而不是死亡的方式。

items.en: Morthor named a secret killing, a death that the killer tried to hide, and the word kept that shadow of concealment.
items.cn: morthor 指私下进行的杀害，是凶手想要掩盖的死亡，这个词一直保留着隐瞒的阴影。

items.en: The verb morthrian meant to commit such a killing, and noun and verb travelled together into later English.
items.cn: 动词 morthrian 意为实施这类杀害，名词和动词一起进入了后来的英语。

items.en: Middle English murdren and murdre referred to both the act and the crime, and the modern spelling settled after the noun.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 murdren 与 murdre，兼指行为和罪名，现代拼写大致在名词之后固定下来。

items.en: Norman French gave English the legal pairing for a killing done with malice, and the courts kept murder apart from manslaughter.
items.cn: 诺曼法语给英语带来了「恶意杀害」的法律搭配，法庭把 murder 与过失杀人清楚分开。

items.en: Modern English keeps the criminal sense and adds a loose everyday sense in which a bad performance or a heavy defeat is called murder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留犯罪义，又加上日常的宽松用法，把糟糕的表演或惨败也称作 murder。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of murder plus two words that merely share its shape; the near-meaning group collects other verbs and legal terms for killing.
note.cn: 形近组收 murder 的同族词，以及两个只是字形接近的词；近义组收其他表示杀害的动词与法律术语。

entries.definition: The person who commits a murder.
entries.definitionCN: 实施谋杀的人。

entries.definition: Capable of or intending to kill; extremely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 有杀人意图的；极其危险的。

entries.definition: To speak quietly under the breath; only the shape resembles murder, the origins differ.
entries.definitionCN: 低声咕哝；只是字形接近 murder，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft, low sound; the spelling is close but the word has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔低沉的声音；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone or something to die.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物死亡。

entries.definition: To kill a prominent person, usually for political reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 通常出于政治原因刺杀要人。

entries.definition: To kill, especially violently, used mostly in old or literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，尤指暴力杀害，多用于古旧或文学作品。

entries.definition: The killing of one person by another, whether lawful or not.
entries.definitionCN: 一人致另一人死亡，无论是否合法。

normalIntro.en: One old English noun of secret killing, its verb and its legal afterlife explain both the crime and the slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词、它的动词，以及它在法律里的延续，同时解释了罪名与俚语。

normal.en: Old English morthor meant a secret killing, so the word begins with concealment rather than with blood.
normal.cn: 古英语 morthor 意为暗中的杀害，所以这个词起点是「隐瞒」，而不是血。

normal.en: Murderer adds -er, the person, while murderous adds -ous, the quality; both stay inside the criminal family.
normal.cn: murderer 加 -er 指人，murderous 加 -ous 指性质，两者都留在犯罪这个词族里。

normal.en: The law keeps murder, deliberate, apart from manslaughter, without intent, and the pair still defines the charge.
normal.cn: 法律把表示故意的 murder 与表示无意的 manslaughter 分开，这一对词至今界定着罪名。

normal.en: Noun and verb share one idea, so you can commit a murder or murder a person with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: 名词与动词共用一个意思，所以 commit a murder 与 murder a person 含义不变。

normal.en: The slang sense survives because murder is extreme, and exaggeration borrows extreme words for bad singing and heavy defeat.
normal.cn: 俚语义能留下来，是因为 murder 足够极端；夸张正好借极端词来形容走调的演唱和惨败。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow pressing another shadow into the ground until it disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子把另一个影子按进地面，直到它消失。

abstract.en: A word for a hidden death reminds you that concealment, not noise, was the original danger.
abstract.cn: 一个表示暗中死亡的词提醒人：最早的危险是掩盖，而不是声响。

abstract.en: Because it names an irreversible act, murder can be borrowed only loosely for a spoiled song or a lost match.
abstract.cn: 因为它指的是一种不可逆的行为，所以只能宽松地借来说糟蹋一首歌或输掉一场比赛。

examples.en: The court found that she had murdered her business partner.
examples.cn: 法庭认定她谋杀了她的生意伙伴。

examples.en: He was charged with murder after the body was found.
examples.cn: 尸体被发现后，他被控谋杀。

examples.en: Our team murdered them in the second half.
examples.cn: 我们队在下半场把他们彻底击败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抹的」——把人从世上抹掉，就是 murder；记住它是谋杀。

root: 古英语 morthor（暗中的杀害）与动词 morthrian 构成，中古英语作 murdre，诺曼法语强化了法律用法；同族词有 murderer、murderous，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a killing kept secret; the senses divide into the crime, the act, the legal charge, and a slang exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是隐秘的杀害；义项分出罪行、行为、法律罪名，以及俚语里的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shadow pressing another shadow flat against the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子把另一个影子按平在地面上。

branches.en: a strip of tape sealing off a dark doorway
branches.cn: 封住黑暗门洞的警戒带

branches.en: a story told to neighbours that nobody believes
branches.cn: 讲给邻居听却没人相信的说法

branches.en: a hand doing what the law forbids
branches.cn: 做了法律禁止之事的那只手

branches.en: a charge read aloud in a courtroom
branches.cn: 法庭上被宣读的一项罪名

branches.en: a song shouted off key into a microphone
branches.cn: 对着麦克风走调喊完的一首歌

intro.en: An Old English noun and verb of secret killing, two English suffixes and the modern compounds carry the entry.
intro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词与动词、两个英语后缀，以及现代复合形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: murder belongs to the Old English stock, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：murder 属于古英语词汇，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。
